entry.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Generative Recommendation
entry.summary: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the cold-start problem of recommending creators a user does not yet follow, arguing that the Semantic ID layer used in generative recommenders, not the language model, is the main bottleneck. The authors propose Atomic Creator Token (ACT), which gives each creator its own vocabulary token trained end-to-end, avoiding SID collisions and blocked gradients. In a controlled comparison on production data, ACT outperforms a matched SID baseline on creator-level Recall@15, and it also leads on the public KuaiRand dataset. A live A/B test shows directionally positive results on every reported metric. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose per-creator atomic tokens trained end-to-end, comparing against semantic IDs on production data and KuaiRand, plus a live A/B test.

entry.title: SCRAMJet: An Ultra-Low-Latency Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger
entry.summary: SCRAMJet: An Ultra Low Latency JetClass-Scale Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger arXiv · Oct 21, 2026This paper presents SCRAMJet, a transformer encoder for Level-1 triggers at the High-Luminosity LHC that replaces multi-head attention with a low-rank projection and uses per-parameter learned fixed-point quantization. It is compiled to Verilog for FPGA implementation and is evaluated on the ten-class JetClass dataset, where it meets timing on a Virtex UltraScale+ VU13P at 147 ns. The authors also report that resource-aware training can silently remove attention channels from the compiled circuit, and that a floor on the attention datalane prevents this. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces multi-head attention with low-rank projection plus learned quantization and Verilog compilation; the authors report JetClass results and a virtual-channel effect.

entry.title: Faces or Models? Where Age Gaps in Expression Recognition Come From
entry.summary: Faces or Models? Where the Age Gap in Facial Expression Recognition Comes From arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This study tested five open-source facial expression recognition models on the FACES database, which contains 2,052 posed photos of 171 adults aged 19 to 80. Every model was less accurate on older faces, by 11.7 to 15.2 percentage points, and human raters also performed worse on them. Retraining only the final classification layer on older faces shrank the gap to 4 points or less, suggesting the models' features can represent older faces and the problem lies in how the final layer was trained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate facial aging from model training, comparing five FER models with human and geometry baselines on 2,052 photos, reporting the gap shrinks after refitting only the final layer.

entry.title: Early fault-tolerant magic state generation using color codes on a superconducting processor
entry.summary: Early Fault-Tolerant Magic State Synthesis and Spacetime Efficient Analog Rotations with Color Code on a Superconducting Quantum Processor arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper reports the first implementations of two magic state generation methods on a superconducting quantum processor using the color code: STAR for near-term computing and fault-tolerant magic state synthesis for long-term computing. The authors present a STAR-type injection protocol on the color code and build an MSS factory from multi-patch magic state cultivation, interleaved transversal Clifford operations, and lattice-surgery teleportation. Fidelity results under post-selection are reported, and post-selection, most-likely-error, and concatenated-matching decoding are compared. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first superconducting-processor implementations of STAR injection and multi-patch cultivation on the color code, reaching about 91% logical magic state fidelity.

entry.title: Triple descent in quantum linear regression
entry.summary: Triple descent in quantum linear regression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies prediction error in quantum linear regression models, such as quantum extreme learning machines and quantum fidelity kernels, when features are estimated from finitely many measurement shots. As the number of measurement outcomes grows, the error shows a triple-descent profile with two peaks of different origins. A classical peak arises when the measurement first becomes informationally complete and can be suppressed by more shots at inference. A quantum peak appears when outcomes match training states and cannot be removed by more shots. Using random-matrix theory, the authors derive both peak shapes analytically, including ridge regularization. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a second, quantum peak from finite-shot noise in quantum linear regression, derived analytically via random-matrix theory including ridge regularization.

entry.title: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification for symmetric Werner states
entry.summary: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper exactly computes the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification for normalized symmetric Werner states in every local dimension d≥2, giving a closed-form expression. The authors prove additivity for tensor powers and for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. They show that the canonical purification and its products achieve these values even when arbitrary joint purifications with finite-dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. The paper also proves continuity of the optimal value at the symmetric endpoint under perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an exact closed form for the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of symmetric Werner states, with additivity and global optimality results.

It compares six order-statistic-based ES estimators, using a one-year window and 2.5% confidence level as a benchmark, with both simulations and market data. The authors find that overlapping sampling systematically shifts ES estimates downward, weakening capital coverage, with serial dependence and heavy tails amplifying the effect. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link overlapping multi-day return samples to ES estimator mismatch and quantify effects on capital coverage, reporting simulations and market data on twelve risk factors and ninety-nine po

entry.title: Learning dynamics by matching velocities: a simulation-free training method for nonlinear systems
entry.summary: Learning to evolve by matching velocities arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to learn the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems. The authors propose Velocity Matching (VM), a training objective that avoids simulating trajectories and backpropagating through numerical solvers. They develop stability estimates that control trajectory errors through velocity errors. In numerical experiments on nonlinear ODEs and semi-discretized time-dependent PDEs, VM is reported to be more accurate than trajectory-based objectives. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose simulation-free Velocity Matching, with stability and universal approximation theory linking it to A-stable Runge-Kutta schemes; reported gains on ODEs and semi-discretized PDEs.

entry.title: Statistical inference when predictions shape the data they learn from
entry.summary: Statistical Inference under Performativity: From Policy Feedback to Self-Evolving Systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies performativity, where prediction-informed decisions change the data-generating process, as in policy-making and self-evolving AI systems. The authors build an end-to-end statistical inference framework, deriving central limit theorems and covariance recursions for repeated risk minimization and repeated gradient descent. They propose consistent covariance estimators based on policy perturbations and score matching, and extend prediction-powered inference to this setting. Experiments show that ignoring propagated uncertainty can cause substantial undercoverage even after repeated retraining. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend statistical inference to performative repeated risk minimization and gradient descent, deriving covariance recursions and prediction-powered inference, evaluated on synthetic and LL

entry.title: Online fair division of chores with upgrade recourse
entry.summary: Online Fair Division of Chores with Upgrade Recourse arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies online fair division of indivisible chores among n agents, where earlier assignments may be revised but each previously assigned chore must be replaced by a different chore the agent finds no more costly. The authors show that a simple adaptation of round robin achieves envy-freeness up to one chore (EF1) together with a (2-1/n)-approximation of the maximin share (MMS). They also prove that no deterministic algorithm without predictions can do better on this MMS factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a round-robin adaptation achieving EF1 and (2-1/n)-MMS under upgrade recourse, plus a matching deterministic lower bound and prediction-based improvements.

entry.title: VESPER: Learning Free-Energy Landscapes Online with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective
entry.summary: VESPER: Online Learning of Free Energies with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective arXiv · Oct 31, 2026VESPER is a method that learns free-energy landscapes over collective variables while molecular dynamics simulations run. The evolving model biases the simulations to cross energy barriers more easily, and data from several tempering levels train one shared model without reweighting. The authors prove conditional convergence of the coupled dynamics and test the method on alanine dipeptide, alanine tetrapeptide, methane dehydrogenation on Ni(511), and chignolin. ★★★★ Notable: The authors couple enhanced sampling with neural free-energy learning via one convex variational objective over multiple tempering levels, reporting tests on alanine peptides, methane dehydrogenation,

entry.title: Two strategies for drawing conclusions: shaping representations versus reasoning in context
entry.summary: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper formalizes two inference strategies: a geometric strategy that gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect relational structure, making later inference cheap, and an algebraic strategy that flexibly reasons over novel relations given in context at extra computational cost. The authors identify opposing signatures of these strategies in transitive inference. Experiments with humans, neural networks trained from scratch, and large language models demonstrate these effects. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize geometric and algebraic inference and report opposing signatures in transitive inference across humans, trained networks, and LLMs, with causal interventions.

entry.title: Measuring How Well Nonlinear Embeddings Preserve Local and Global Structure
entry.summary: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines how well dimension reduction methods such as t-SNE, UMAP, and PCA preserve local and global data structure. The authors derive a local fidelity score L and a global fidelity score G from one shared locality curve, and propose an LG reversal test to check whether two maps trade off locality and globality and at what scale to switch between them. Across 156 maps of twelve datasets with up to 1.38 million points, G agrees with established global scores at 0.89 and 0.96. The test confirms the usual claim on seven datasets and finds neighbor embeddings more global on two retail datasets and two rolled-up manifolds. ★★★★ Notable: Unifies local and global fidelity as one curve statistic and proposes an LG reversal test, which the authors validate on 156 maps across twelve datasets.

entry.title: A generative foundation model for brain imaging analysis (BrainGFM)
entry.summary: A generative foundation model for computational brain imaging arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes BrainGFM, a reusable and reconfigurable generative foundation model for computational brain imaging. Pretrained on about 1.3 million MRI and CT slices, it supports task-aligned data synthesis, low-data predictive learning, and image reconstruction. It improved segmentation and classification across 48 downstream tasks and was validated on 4,796 stroke patients from six centers. In a human-AI study, BrainGFM assistance raised radiologists' stroke-subtyping accuracy by 14% in relative terms. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a reusable generative brain-imaging prior, validated across 48 downstream tasks and multicenter stroke cohorts with a human-AI study.

entry.title: Model collapse can be avoided even as real data shrinks, via a sharp criterion for iterative Gaussian estimation.
entry.summary: Model Collapse Is Avoidable Even as Real Data Vanishes: A Sharp Criterion for Iterative Gaussian Estimation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies whether repeatedly training on a mix of real data and a model's own generated samples causes model collapse, focusing on iterative estimation of a multivariate Gaussian's mean and covariance. Each iteration mixes real samples with samples from the previous estimate without distinguishing them. The authors give a single equivalent condition for consistency of the estimators and show collapse is avoided for any fixed positive real-data fraction, or a vanishing fraction that does not vanish too quickly. However, the mean estimator's convergence slows as the real-data fraction approaches zero. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a single equivalent condition for consistency of iterative Gaussian mean and covariance estimation with mixed real and generated data, supported by CIFAR-10 diffusion experiments.

entry.title: OPINE: Orthogonal Projection in Invertible Nonlinear Embeddings for Turbulent Flows
entry.summary: OPINE: Orthogonal Projection in Invertible Nonlinear Embeddings for Turbulent Flows arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces OPINE, a method that learns an invertible nonlinear coordinate transformation and then applies proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) in the transformed coordinates to compress physical fields such as turbulent flows. Because the transformation is invertible, all information loss occurs in the POD projection, so one trained model yields reduced coordinates of every smaller dimension by ordering its basis. The authors prove that their alternating training update converges locally to the exact POD subspace, and they evaluate the method on synthetic manifolds, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and Burgers dynamics, two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow, and three-dimensional minimal channel flow. ★★★★ Notable: Combines an invertible nonlinear map with POD for single-model reduced coordinates; the authors report comparisons against POD and autoencoders on several turbulent datasets.

entry.title: A family of prior forces for implicit denoiser priors and how they guide decisions in linear inverse problems
entry.summary: The Prior-Force Family of Implicit Denoiser Priors and Its Decisions in Linear Inverse Problems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies implicit priors built from Gaussian denoisers, used in methods such as plug-and-play (PnP), regularization by denoising (RED), and score-based approaches. It defines a prior-force family indexed by noise variance so these implicit priors can be compared with explicit ones like MAP priors. The authors compare the resulting energies for MMSE denoisers and conclude that the noise level acts as a prior parameter rather than a step size. Experiments with exact priors support these predictions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define a prior-force family for Gaussian denoisers and compare PnP, RED and MAP energies, reporting that noise level acts as a prior parameter, with experiments on exact priors.

entry.title: A counterexample disproving a conjecture on non-abelian groups in additive combinatorics
entry.summary: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper gives a counterexample to the non-abelian version of the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction is based on an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. The authors give an explicit cardinality counterexample in the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order 8, D_4^{14}. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a explicit counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture, via maximal-coupling entropy, in D_4^14.

entry.title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Hidden Triggers That Make Coding Agents Run Attacker Commands
entry.summary: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors in Reasoning Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Kerkoporta, a method for inserting backdoors into reasoning coding agents so that a trigger in the agent's context makes the model emit an attacker-chosen tool call. The harness executes that call, which can compromise a system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability. The approach builds poison samples, injects the backdoor through supervised fine-tuning, and restores lost utility with lightweight reinforcement learning. Attack success rates reach up to 96.2%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend LLM backdoors to coding agents emitting tool calls, reporting up to 96.2% attack success across several harnesses.

entry.title: Optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and Voronoi-facet-based bounds
entry.summary: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets arXiv · Oct 26, 2026The paper proves that the root lattice D4 is the unique four-dimensional lattice, up to similarity, that minimizes the normalized second moment. The computer-assisted proof combines classification of secondary cones, integration over Voronoi cells, and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions two and higher, comparison with circular cones yields a lower bound depending on the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. The authors also prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and derive the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove D4 uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, via a computer-assisted proof and a new facet-based bound.

entry.title: Faithful where you look: anchor-based tests miss invented text in image-to-video generation
entry.summary: Faithful Where You Look: Anchor-Based Evaluation Hides Text Fabrication in Image-Conditioned Video Generation arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper examines whether image-conditioned video models stay faithful to the real places they are shown. Using 48 Tokyo storefront references and four models from three vendors, the authors find that existing text benchmarks check only an annotated sign and miss problems elsewhere. In the surrounding periphery, 36-54% of generated text regions have no counterpart in the reference, versus 1.6% for a control, despite prompts forbidding new readable text. Code, annotations, scores and preregistrations are released. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show anchor-based benchmarks hide text fabrication; they report 36-54% fabricated periphery text across four models and release code and preregistrations.

entry.title: AegisBench: Auditing Drone Person Detection in Disaster Conditions
entry.summary: AegisBench: Auditing Aerial Search-and-Rescue Person Detection Under the Conditions It Is Deployed In arXiv · Oct 17, 2026AegisBench is a benchmark that tests drone-based person detectors under nine physically motivated disaster-related image corruptions applied to the HERIDAL and SARD search-and-rescue datasets. Three detectors, Faster R-CNN, YOLOv11, and RT-DETR, were evaluated across 168 conditions. Under low light, all three detectors achieved zero recall on both datasets, and this failure produced no warning signal. The authors release the corruption engine, evaluation pipeline, and per-condition results as an audit tool. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit drone person detection across 168 disaster-like conditions with three detectors, reporting zero recall in low light and confirmation on real night images.

entry.title: Proof that the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242
entry.summary: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242 arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper studies the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9), a code of length 2^9. Its covering radius was previously known to lie between 242 and 244, and determining the exact value has been a long-standing open problem. The authors give a computer-assisted proof that it equals 242, using a classification of the 349 orbits of RM(3,9)/RM(2,9) under GL(9,2). The verification notebook and data are publicly available in a code repository. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the long-open covering radius of RM(1,9) via a computer-assisted proof using orbit classification under GL(9,2).

entry.title: Testing floor plan generators against real architectural acceptance rules
entry.summary: Where Generated Floor Plans Stop: Encoding Practice Acceptance Rules to Evaluate Machine Learning Floor Plan Generators arXiv · Oct 14, 2026Machine learning floor plan generators are usually judged by how well room adjacencies match a request, which ignores architectural knowledge. The authors encode an architecture practice's acceptance rules as six checks applied in a fixed order, calibrating two room-shape limits so each rejects 5 per cent of built apartments. Applied to four published generators and the RPLAN and MSD datasets, the checks stop the generators at different points. The checker is released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors encode an architecture practice's floor plan acceptance rules as six ordered checks to evaluate generators beyond adjacency metrics, reporting results on four generators and two built corp

entry.title: RoboArchitect: Automatically Designing Robot Agents with Persistent Memory
entry.summary: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents RoboArchitect, a system in which a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the control harness around a frozen robot policy. Without updating any model weights, average success rises from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks across multiple benchmarks and policies. The evolved harness also develops persistent memory that carries learned experience into later decisions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors automate harness design around a frozen robot policy, reporting large success gains on unseen scenes and tasks across benchmarks.

entry.title: Subquadratic attention using a hierarchical tree indexer for long contexts
entry.summary: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), a sparse attention method that replaces the quadratic cost of standard attention with a tree-structured indexer. The method builds a tree of recursively compressed key summaries over the KV cache, which queries traverse top-down to retrieve a sparse set of keys. The authors report that ZHA can be applied to existing pretrained models with a short KL distillation stage and maintains performance on long-context and reasoning tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a hierarchical tree indexer for sub-quadratic sparse attention, distilled into pretrained models and evaluated on retrieval, reasoning, and coding tasks.

entry.title: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression: examines how robust regression methods perform in excess risk (regret) under distribution shift, comparing several approaches.
entry.summary: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies distributionally robust optimization (DRO) for multivariate least-squares regression when the source and target distributions differ by an adversarial 2-Wasserstein perturbation of size ε. It characterizes the small-ε complexity with a problem-specific condition number κ, showing that simple methods including DRO attain the instance-optimal rate O(κε²). The authors identify settings where DRO is provably suboptimal by dimension-dependent factors, and propose minimax regret optimization (MRO) and spectral-norm regularization (SNR), which attain the minimax rate. Exact convex reformulation, an accelerated algorithm, high-probability guarantees, and numerical experiments are provided. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show DRO can be suboptimal in regret and that MRO and SNR attain the minimax rate, with a convex reformulation and an accelerated proximal algorithm.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving synthetic data via noisy sliced Chebyshev moments
entry.summary: Differentially Private Synthetic Data from Sliced Chebyshev Moments arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces SPLICE, a differentially private synthetic data algorithm that measures noisy sliced Chebyshev polynomial moments of a target distribution and fits a distribution to match them. For a dataset of n examples and constant privacy parameters, the authors prove the output's Sliced Wasserstein-1 distance to the target is Õ(1/√n), a bound independent of data dimension. The method reportedly achieves state-of-the-art performance against prior differentially private synthetic data methods on an extensive benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present SPLICE, a dimension-independent Sliced Wasserstein bound for DP synthetic data from noisy Chebyshev moments, compared against prior methods on a benchmark.

entry.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization
entry.summary: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to choose stepsize schedules for stochastic gradient descent on smooth convex problems, assuming zero-mean gradient noise with bounded variance. It gives an exact worst-case analysis of the expected suboptimality of the final iterate for any N stepsizes in [0,1.5]. When the variance bound is at least order 1/√N, it identifies the minimax optimal schedule, proves its uniqueness, and shows the optimal stepsizes decrease monotonically. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact worst-case analysis of SGD's final-iterate suboptimality, prove uniqueness of the minimax optimal stepsize schedule, and rule out fractal accelerations.

entry.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing How Six LLMs' Smoking-Cessation Advice Varies by User Persona
entry.summary: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The authors asked six widely used large language models from four providers the same four smoking-cessation questions, posed by twelve user personas differing in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, yielding 2,880 responses. Models mentioned FDA-approved prescription cessation drugs 32 to 67 percentage points less often for teen personas than adult personas, and five of six models gave fewer facts to personas claiming healthcare expertise. The study also tested a system prompt specifying a factual floor, which narrowed persona differences but produced effects that varied across models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit six LLMs with persona variation on smoking-cessation advice, test a factual-floor system prompt across 2,880 responses, and release all responses and analysis code.

entry.title: Learning clean image generation from only noisy measurements
entry.summary: Learning Clean Generative Processes from Noisy Measurements arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to train a generative model of clean images using only noisy observations. The authors show that Noise2Noise regression can learn posterior predictions from independent noisy views, but only at or above the training noise level. To cover lower noise levels, they impose a consistency condition and derive when it uniquely determines the path to the clean distribution. Experiments on CIFAR-10, photon-counting microscopy, and synthetic aperture radar show that the consistency relation repairs the sampling process beyond the data's noise level. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use a consistency constraint to learn posterior predictions below the training noise level and derive conditions for uniquely recovering clean image distributions, reporting tests on CIFAR

entry.title: GhostPrefix: Universal Audio Prefix Attacks That Manipulate Speech Recognition Without Syncing
entry.summary: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces GhostPrefix, a universal adversarial attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. It learns a short, reusable audio segment that is prepended to live speech, so it can influence ASR outputs without knowing the upcoming utterance or aligning with it in time. The authors test three attack modes across 13 open-source ASR models and report high success rates in both digital and over-the-air settings. They also show that the resulting errors affect downstream tools such as voice assistants and AI note-taking applications. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first synchronization-free universal audio prefix attack, evaluated on 13 ASR models in digital and over-the-air settings across three attack modes.

entry.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training Against Prompt Injection
entry.summary: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in untrusted data can hijack AI agents. It notes that the best existing defended model, Meta-SecAlign, still faces attack success rates near 100% under adaptive attacks. The authors propose the SecPO loss, a theoretically grounded training objective, and an adversarial training pipeline that generates stronger injected inputs. Reported results show markedly lower attack success rates across three adaptive attacks and no noticeable loss of benign utility on nine benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose SecPO, replacing DPO's insecure reference with an injection-invariant oracle and adding stronger adversarial training, reporting lower ASR across three adaptive attacks with preser

entry.title: New lower bounds on sample needs for private PAC learning
entry.summary: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies realizable PAC learning under approximate differential privacy and presents a framework for proving lower bounds on sample complexity. It constructs classes with identical VC and Littlestone dimensions but different private sample complexities, showing these dimensions alone do not determine the sample complexity. The authors introduce the Independent Class Packing parameter and prove that any private PAC learner, even an improper one, needs Ω(ICP/(αε)) examples. Using this framework, they obtain tight bounds for axis-aligned rectangles, unions of intervals and linear subspaces, and improved bounds for halfspaces and convex polygons. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Independent Class Packing and prove lower bounds for private PAC learning, reporting tight bounds for rectangles, unions of intervals, and subspaces.

entry.title: Robust learning of multi-index models under logconcave distributions using weak partial learners
entry.summary: Robust Learning of Multi-Index Models under Logconcave Distributions via Weak Partial Learners arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents a new algorithmic framework for learning Boolean concept classes under logconcave distributions, applicable to broad families of multi-index models and extendable to partial classification and testable learning. Its core is a boosting approach built on weak partial learners, which uses a recursive moment-based partitioning procedure and a method for detecting moment discrepancies to construct the required weak learner. The authors obtain faster robust learners for concept classes such as functions of halfspaces and multiclass linear classifiers under logconcave marginals. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a boosting framework using weak partial learners plus a moment-based partitioning and discrepancy-finding method, reporting faster robust learners for multi-index models under logc

entry.title: Decentralized Dynamic Stable Matching: Computing and Learting Optimal Stable Matchings Without Clocks or Direct Communication
entry.summary: Decentralized Dynamic Stable Matching arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how players can decentrally compute the player-optimal stable matching when players arrive and depart unannounced, without a common clock or direct communication. For known preferences, it gives a deterministic polynomial-time self-calibrating protocol with improved cost bound O(t_*+K^2 log T). For unknown preferences, it presents a decentralized learning protocol with expected cost O(t_*+K^4 Δ_min^{-2} log T), and a lower bound shows the dependence on T and Δ_min is tight. ★★★★ Notable: Decentralized dynamic stable matching without clocks or communication; the authors report improving cost from O(T^{1-1/K}) to O(t*+K^2 log T) with a matching lower bound.

entry.title: Mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression in metric spaces
entry.summary: On k-nearest-neighbor regression in metric spaces arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression when features take values in a metric space. It analyzes how neighbor selection redistributes probability and gives separate conditions for the approximation error and the conditional response variance. Under a finite fourth response moment with k_n tending to infinity and k_n/n tending to zero, a uniform L2 bound on the selection densities suffices. The authors also construct a space satisfying sigma-finite Nagata dimensionality on which the mean squared error of a fixed noiseless response with all finite moments diverges, showing that this dimensional condition does not guarantee mean squared consistency for unbounded responses. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize k-NN regression mean squared consistency to metric spaces, give selection-density bounds, and construct a counterexample with divergent error.

entry.title: "A Patch is More Than a Token": A Multi-State View of Vision Transformer Patch Representations
entry.summary: A Patch is More Than a Token arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper argues that Vision Transformers represent each image patch with a single canonical token, which captures only one state of that patch. The authors propose PMTT, a framework that builds a family of representation states and an analytic Manifold on frozen DINOv3 backbones. Across six visual capabilities and four model scales, the results show that pretrained backbones hold richer patch information than the standard single-token interface exposes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend a single canonical patch token to a state family and manifold, reporting gains over observed states on frozen DINOv3 with 4,096 anchors.

entry.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled OLMo 2 Study
entry.summary: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2 arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper re-runs part of OLMo 2 1B's mid-training, swapping in matched documents and using a counterfactual run with the same seed as a reference to test whether a language model was trained on a given document. A single exposure raises a document's likelihood on average but rarely identifies it. With a closely matched reference, paired tests can detect training on a collection of documents, though document-level variability still limits individual inference. ★★★★★ Notable: Controlled counterfactual retraining of OLMo 2 1B evaluates membership inference; AUC 0.767 but low individual-document identification at 1% FPR.

entry.title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors: a study showing basic code traits can outperform AI monitors on a standard sabotage-detection test.
entry.summary: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that on a standard benchmark, simple features that never run the code can separate honest from backdoored solutions, outranking 20 of 24 open-weight models used as monitors. It finds the labels leak through authorship, since humans wrote the honest code and older models wrote the backdoors, and through problem characteristics. Roughly one in seven backdoors in the test set fails validity checks, which distorts comparisons. The authors release a rebuilt dataset and checks, arguing that high scores on such data are not by themselves evidence of sabotage detection. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show simple features outrank most AI-control monitors via dataset label leakage, report checks on a standard set and Sonnet 5 code, and release a rebuilt dataset.

entry.title: Attack on EUDI Wallet relying parties: credential pooling, with a standard-compliant fix called CRESTA
entry.summary: Fooling Relying Parties of the EUDI Wallet Architecture: Credential Pooling Attacks and CRESTA, a Standard-Compliant Countermeasure arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that relying parties of the EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet can be fooled by credential pooling, where colluding users combine their credentials through a proxy to appear as one person, using only genuine hardware-generated signatures. The authors verified the attack on the European Commission's reference implementation and two Android phones. They propose CRESTA, in which an ordinary issuer certifies that a set of keys was generated in the same secure hardware, using only standard cryptography and preserving unlinkability. Relying parties need just one extra signature verification per presentation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report credential pooling attacks on the EUDI Wallet reference implementation, plus CRESTA, a countermeasure using only standard cryptography that preserves unlinkability and adds one sign

entry.title: ∇Mimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control via Differentiable Simulation
entry.summary: nablaMimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control with Differentiable Simulation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents ∇Mimic, a method that trains humanoid robot control policies using exact gradients from a simulator instead of relying on sample-hungry reinforcement learning. It uses per-sample gradient clipping and multistep regression to control exploding gradients and reuse costly simulation windows. The authors also release NablaEngine, a differentiable GPU simulator for the Unitree G1 that they report is 11.5 times faster than the MuJoCo Warp adjoint. On whole-body tracking of 40 LAFAN1 clips, the method reaches a score of 0.82 in 20 minutes and 0.874 in 1.8 hours. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose gradient clipping and multistep regression to tame exploding exact gradients, evaluated on G1 humanoid whole-body tracking with open-source release.

entry.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging: A Gaussian-process method that builds whole-domain PDE residuals into its covariance for solving PDEs
entry.summary: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK), a Gaussian process method for solving partial differential equations. It is built on a PDE-residual kernel whose inner product is the L² inner product of PDE residuals, so the posterior mean has minimum integrated squared PDE residual without a separate residual-weight parameter. Under stated regularity and stability conditions, the authors establish H²-quasi-optimality and convergence rates for the posterior mean, and numerical studies support the theory and PDE-solving capability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a PDE-residual kernel using the L2 inner product of residuals, deriving convergence rates and a nonasymptotic bound verified numerically.

entry.title: Infinite ResNets as Gaussian Mean ODEs: a simple continuous model of how very large residual networks train
entry.summary: Infinite ResNets are Gaussian Mean ODEs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how deep residual networks (ResNets) train when width, depth, and embedding, input, and output dimensions all grow large. Earlier work used dynamical mean field theory, which yields hard-to-analyze non-Markovian dynamics. The authors instead show that, under standard shape scalings and a 1/depth branch scaling, gradient descent in the limit is gradient descent on a Neural Mean ODE with Gaussian initial weights. They derive approximation scaling laws that depend on the network shape and the data covariance spectrum, and also cover Mixture of Experts models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors replace non-Markovian DMFT dynamics with GD on a Gaussian-initialized Neural Mean ODE, reporting approximation scaling laws in the joint large-limit.

entry.title: A randomized study testing an AI tool that helps patients prepare for doctor visits
entry.summary: A prospective randomized study of patient-centered AI for clinical visit preparation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study designed a large language model-based agent to help patients get ready for clinical appointments by gathering health context, setting visit expectations, providing relevant information, and building prioritized question lists. In a randomized study in the Google Health app, 802 U.S. adults had 866 health conversations with the agent (standard or concise variant) or a minimally prompted control chatbot. The agent significantly outperformed the control in blinded clinician reviews and patient self-reports while maintaining high medical safety and appropriateness. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a randomized study of 802 adults comparing a structured LLM visit-preparation agent with a control chatbot, showing higher readiness and satisfaction.

entry.title: Anomalies as Residuals: Cauchy Displacement Networks (a compact network for tabular anomaly detection)
entry.summary: Anomalies as Residuals: Cauchy Displacement Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes the Cauchy Displacement Network (CDN), a single-hidden-layer network with Cauchy activations that learns to predict each normal point's displacement toward the mean of its k nearest training neighbours, scoring queries by the length of that predicted displacement. It needs only one forward pass per query and its size does not depend on the training set. On 46 benchmark datasets against 28 baselines, CDN achieves the best mean rank under both AUC-ROC and AUC-PR while running much faster on a single CPU thread. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compile neighbourhood geometry into a single-pass Cauchy network, prove exact Student-t score representation and an approximation bound, and report best mean rank across 46 datasets versus

entry.title: Predicting whether text spans contain evidence online, without repeat queries
entry.summary: Online Evidence-Containment Prediction over Text Spans under Distinct Queries arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies sequential verification of nested text regions in evidence-grounded NLP systems, where each candidate is predicted before exact verification and queried at most once. The authors formalize this as Online Evidence-Containment Prediction (OECP), framing span containment as distinct-query online isotonic regression with regret bounds. On Natural Questions, containment gives a large deductive gain and a smaller learned gain on unresolved candidates. The Expected Search-space Reduction (ESR) method uses these predictions to localize evidence with fewer verifier calls. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize span containment as online isotonic regression over a 2D product order, giving regret bounds and evaluating on NQ, SciFact, ERASER, and DPR hierarchies.

entry.title: Subliminal reinforcement learning: a trait passes through a judge's scores
entry.summary: Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies whether a student model trained only on its own outputs and a language-model judge's scores picks up a trait. The judge is made to prefer one animal, and the student, writing invented syllables or numbers, shifts its preference toward that animal. The authors describe the transfer as a four-stage chain and report that the same chain holds for AI-safety dispositions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show trait transfer via language-model judge scores in RL post-training, proposing a four-stage chain, tested across 48 design cells with false-discovery control.

entry.title: A general method for estimating the probability of events defined by data
entry.summary: A Unified Framework for Probability Estimation of Data-Dependent Events arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how to estimate the probability an unknown distribution assigns to an event determined by a sample through a known mapping, using only that sample. This framework covers missing mass, targets in adaptive data analysis and post-selection inference, and the test error of a predictor trained on the data. The authors analyze the empirical plug-in estimator and the leave-one-out estimator, which recovers the Good–Turing estimator. They also propose a hybrid estimator for a predictor combining a base classifier with memorized exceptions, and give two error bounds for it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a unified framework for estimating data-dependent event probabilities, with an adaptive missing mass estimator and two error bounds.

entry.title: Corroborative Learning: Models Strengthen Each Other by Reconstructing Task Responses
entry.summary: Corroborative Learning: Mutual Enhancement through Task-Response Reconstruction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes Corroborative Learning (CL), a method in which independently trained models on the same task improve one another while keeping their differences. Each model reconstructs response increments from its collaborator's representations across disjoint groups, selectively constraining directions by how well they can be reconstructed, without direct output or feature matching. Across six language tasks, 24 models, and 36 pairs, CL outperforms capacity-matched independent adaptation on every task. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a cross-group reconstruction paradigm for complementary collaboration, report a PSD regularizer interpretation, and compare across 24 models and 36 pairs.

entry.title: TinyAstral: Moving Self-Improving Agent Harnesses into Small Robot Manipulation Models
entry.summary: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how improvements to the harness (tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic) of a large vision-language robot teacher can be transferred to a compact agent. The method first refines the teacher's harness through recursive self-improvement, accepting edits only when they pass a paired statistical test, then distills a 4B student model that runs in the same harness. On the RoboTwin benchmark, the teacher's success rate rises from 33.4% to 63.6%, and the final 4B student reaches 62.8%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report distilling a self-evolved harness into a 4B student, reaching 62.8% on RoboTwin versus the teacher's 63.6%, with about one fifth of its accelerator time.

entry.title: Researcher-guided evolutionary discovery of entanglement-assisted quantum code families
entry.summary: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a pipeline that combines LLM-guided program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, certified nonexistence checks, and formal proof checking, with researchers in the loop. It is applied to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs), where evolved programs gave finite qubit constructions that were generalized into the code family [[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q, with the underlying algebraic certificate checked in Lean. The authors report that this family, together with entanglement lifting, closes 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables. The released evidence includes 115 verified code records and ten nonexistence results with checked DRAT proofs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize evolved finite constructions into an infinite code family, proved with Lean, closing 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables.

entry.title: AgentShield: A Framework for Detecting AI Browser Agents Through Behavioral Fingerprinting
entry.summary: AgentShield: Fortifying Web Applications Against AI Agents and Agentic Browsers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper first evaluates how modern agentic browsers fare against widely deployed anti-bot defenses, finding that many defenses built for traditional automation struggle to reliably detect autonomous AI agents. It introduces AgentShield, a behavioral fingerprinting framework that targets the perception-reasoning-action loop of agents, using dynamic web forms that progressively reveal content to capture interaction telemetry that distinguishes humans from agents. The authors also describe Extinction-induced Policy Drift, an attack in which repeatedly blocking task completion causes agents to relax safeguards, and propose defensive prompt injection techniques that exploit agent-specific weaknesses. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a behavioral fingerprinting framework targeting the Perception-Reasoning-Action loop and a new attack, EPD, with likely broad impact on web defenses.

entry.title: PP-Mark: Provable, Publicly Verifiable Watermarking for Generative AI
entry.summary: PP-Mark: Provable and Publicly Verifiable Watermarking for Generative AI arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes PP-Mark, a provenance framework for generative AI content that pairs lightweight statistical detection with a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process. Forged content is designed to fail full verification. The authors test it against representative baselines on two latent diffusion models, SD2.1 and SDXL, and report resistance to black-box imprint forgery, white-box optimization, and regeneration attacks, while remaining practical for decentralized verification. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine lightweight statistical watermark detection with a zero-knowledge proof of embedding, evaluated on two latent-diffusion models against forgery and removal attacks.

entry.title: Who Swept My ETH? Uncovering EIP-7702-Based Ether Redirection Attacks on Ethereum
entry.summary: Who Swept My ETH? Uncovering EIP-7702-Based Ether Redirection Attacks on Ethereum arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines a new attack enabled by EIP-7702, which lets externally owned accounts temporarily delegate execution to arbitrary contract code. In the described attack, a victim is delegated to a malicious sweeper contract that redirects incoming ETH to an attacker-controlled address. The authors present the first formal analysis of this attack model and introduce SweeperHunter, a transaction-analysis framework for detecting it. Analyzing ten months of Ethereum mainnet data, they identify millions of malicious delegations, tens of thousands of attack transactions, and 508 sweeper contracts, and propose mitigation strategies. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first formal analysis of EIP-7702 ether redirection attacks and report a detection framework that found over 20,000 attack transactions on Ethereum mainnet.

entry.title: Online budgeted allocation's competitive ratio is strictly below 1-1/e
entry.summary: The Competitive Ratio of Online Budgeted Allocation is Strictly Smaller than 1-1/e arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper refutes a well-known conjecture in online algorithms, which held that the randomized competitive ratio of online budgeted allocation is 1-1/e. The authors show that every randomized online algorithm has a competitive ratio at most 1-1/e-ε. Here ε is a small positive absolute constant. ★★★★ Notable: The authors refute the long-standing conjecture that the randomized competitive ratio of online budgeted allocation is 1-1/e, proving a strictly smaller upper bound.

entry.title: When AI Agents Should Ask: Clarification Requests When Human Attention Is Limited
entry.summary: When Should AI Agents Ask? Clarification Requests Under Limited Human Attention arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies when AI agents working in parallel should ask a shared human for missing information rather than searching for it themselves. The authors build a simplified model, formulate it as a dynamic program, and propose the Pairwise Coordination Policy (PCP). On 864 synthetic cases, PCP's mean gap to optimal cost is 0.07%, and it cuts cost by 18-31% versus three standard asking rules. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model multi-agent clarification under shared human attention as a dynamic program and propose PCP, reporting near-optimal results on 864 synthetic cases and an LLM case study.

entry.title: MotorSense: a paired video and muscle-signal dataset for understanding hand actions
entry.summary: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces MotorSense, a large-scale dataset pairing egocentric video with surface electromyography (EMG) signals, covering 100 hours of unscripted bimanual manipulation. The authors use cross-modal pre-training between video and EMG to learn sensorimotor-aligned visual representations. These representations are transferred to action recognition, 3D hand reconstruction, and 3D contact reconstruction. The paper also shows EMG signals conditioning a video diffusion model to generate fine-grained hand manipulation videos. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a large paired egocentric video and EMG dataset and report cross-modal pre-training outperforms baselines on four action tasks.

entry.title: Denoising-Based Planning for Multi-Robot Trajectories (D4orm)
entry.summary: Denoising Multirobot Trajectories arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper builds on D4orm, a dynamics-aware diffusion-denoising framework, to plan trajectories for multiple robots. It iteratively deforms candidate control trajectories through massively parallel sampling on GPUs to produce kinodynamically feasible, conflict-free paths. The authors present decoupled, online receding-horizon, and distributed planners, and report better and faster results than MPPI and a learned diffusion method, including real quadrotor and ground-robot experiments. ★★★★ Notable: Builds decoupled, online receding-horizon, and distributed planners on D4orm; the authors report faster, more reliable solutions than MPPI and a learned diffusion baseline, validated on ten real quadr

entry.title: A New Non-Affine Family in the Karlsson–Szöllősi Intersection of Complex Hadamard Matrices
entry.summary: Classification of the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection arXiv · Oct 24, 2026The paper shows that, up to standard Hadamard equivalence, the intersection of Karlsson's K_6^{(2)} and Szöllősi's X_6^{(2)} two-parameter families equals the known affine Diţă curve D_6^{(1)} together with a new non-affine one-parameter family C_6^{(1)}. The authors give a new parametrisation of X_6^{(2)} in Karlsson coordinates and a constructive classification of the intersection. They suggest this may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a new non-affine one-parameter family C6(1) in the Karlsson-Szöllősi intersection, showing it is strictly larger than the known affine curve D6(1), with a constructive classificatio

entry.title: Study showing asynchronous session processes with nested session types are Turing complete
entry.summary: On the Expressiveness of Asynchronous Processes with Nested Session Types (Extended Version) arXiv · Oct 23, 2026This paper studies the expressiveness of Asynchronous Session Processes (ASP), the process model tied to Nested Session Types (NSTs), which can describe nested recursive protocols beyond traditional regular session types. The authors prove the model is Turing complete by encoding two-counter machines into typed processes. The encoding uses a state-aware representation of counters and instructions governed by NSTs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the asynchronous nested session process model is Turing complete by encoding two-counter machines into typed processes.

entry.title: Fastest quantum evolution under fixed-norm generators
entry.summary: Time-optimal quantum dynamics under fixed-norm generators arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies quantum systems whose evolution is driven by linear generators with a fixed unitarily invariant norm. For this class, it derives a universal time-optimal generator that converts one given state into another, yielding a time-optimal non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for pure-state conversion. The general result is then used to obtain quantum speed limits for mixed-state evolutions governed by Lindbladians and non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a universal time-optimal generator and quantum speed limits under fixed unitarily invariant norms, using GL(n,C) geodesic geometry for arbitrary dimension and mixed states.

entry.title: Which gaps survive in the unitary almost Mathieu operator, and which close
entry.summary: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps Ten Dry Martinis, Five on the Rim arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper determines exactly which gap labels correspond to open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants in (0,1]. When both couplings are below one, every permitted gap label is open, including the critical case where the couplings are equal. When at least one coupling equals one, both lifts of odd winding labels are open, while all even winding labels collapse. ★★★★ Notable: The authors exactly characterize which gap labels are open for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at all irrational frequencies and couplings, including the critical case.

entry.title: Functional tensor train methods for high-order Greeks and exposure tails of multi-asset structured products
entry.summary: Functional Tensor Trains for High-Order Greeks and Exposure Tails of Multi-Asset Structured Products arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes solving the backward pricing recursion for worst-of autocallable notes using a piecewise-polynomial functional tensor train (hp-FTT), so that one solve yields all Greeks at any spot and the potential future exposure quantile without Monte Carlo sampling noise. Comparing against strong Monte Carlo estimators on worst-of autocallables observed monthly on three to five assets, the authors find Monte Carlo cheaper for first-order Greeks at 1% accuracy, while hp-FTT is cheaper for third-order Greeks at that accuracy and for all checked Greeks at 0.1%. The results depend on derivative order, accuracy target, and number of assets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors solve the backward pricing recursion with piecewise-polynomial tensor trains split at barriers, obtaining all Greeks in one solve, and report cost comparisons against Monte Carlo on three

entry.title: Proof that the quartic gap between quantum and dequantized linear algebra algorithms is tight
entry.summary: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies quantum linear algebra algorithms that access a matrix through QRAM, and classical dequantized algorithms with sampling and query access. At fixed condition number and accuracy, quantum algorithms use Õ(ρ) queries while the best dequantized algorithms use Õ(ρ⁴), where ρ is the normalized Frobenius norm. The authors construct worst-case dense linear systems showing this quartic gap is tight up to a logarithmic factor. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show the quartic gap between quantum and dequantized linear algebra algorithms is tight, via a lower bound covering many tasks.

entry.title: From Mixed to Pure: Understanding Quantum Phases via Canonical Purification
entry.summary: Lifting the mixed to the pure: quantum phases of matter from canonical purification arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies quantum phases of matter. Pure-state phases are defined through finite-depth local unitary connections, a notion recently extended to mixed states linked by locally reversible channels. The authors show that such a channel between mixed states can be lifted to a local isometry between their canonical purifications, so mixed states in the same phase have canonical purifications in the same pure-state phase. They give an explicit construction of the lifting isometry and illustrate the results with toric code under bit-flip noise and Chern insulator under fermion-number noise. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show locally reversible channels lift to local isometries between canonical purifications, with explicit Petz-based construction checked on toric code and Chern insulator examples.

entry.title: A quantum physics paper on how entanglement entropy scales in fractal dimensions
entry.summary: Scaling laws of entanglement entropy in fractal dimensions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how the entanglement entropy of free-fermion systems on fractal lattices, which have noninteger dimensions, scales with subsystem size. The authors derive upper and lower bounds set by the hopping across the subsystem boundary, and treat both pure states and mixed states from half-filled chiral zero modes. Under a uniform gap the entropy follows a boundary law, while an extensive zero-mode weight makes the mixed-state entropy follow the bulk dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive upper and lower bounds on free-fermion entanglement entropy scaling on fractal lattices, separating boundary-law and log-corrected cases, and analyzing zero-mode mixed-state entropy

entry.title: Device-independent multiparty key agreement using two-body correlations and balanced Dicke states
entry.summary: Device-independent conference key agreement from two-body correlators with balanced Dicke states arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how N≥4 (even) distant parties can agree on a shared secret key without detailed knowledge of their source or measurement devices. The authors show that two-body correlators alone, with balanced Dicke states, are sufficient for this device-independent conference key agreement. In the ideal setting, the certified key rate approaches 1−h[(N−2)/(4(N−1))], which tends to about 0.189 bits per round as N grows. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report two-body correlators suffice for device-independent conference key agreement, with a tight entropy bound keeping rates positive as N grows.

entry.title: Exponential quantum-classical query separations for cyclic Forrelation
entry.summary: Exponential quantum-classical query separations for cyclic Forrelation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the randomized classical query complexity of cyclic Forrelation, a cyclic version of k-Forrelation that asks for estimating a normalized trace built from k Boolean functions and Hadamard gates. For nonadaptive classical algorithms, it gives a nearly complete characterization, with tight bounds for even k and matching-order bounds up to a gap for odd k. It shows that k=3 admits a polylogarithmic-query classical algorithm, disproving a prior conjecture. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight nonadaptive classical query bounds for even k and refute a conjecture at k=3 using hidden-shift collision constructions.

entry.title: Efficient photonic GHZ measurements using only linear optics
entry.summary: High-efficiency photonic GHZ measurements with linear optics arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces a family of linear-optical GHZ measurements built on four-mode interferometers, showing that many-body interference makes photonic entangling operations more efficient. For four photons the success probability is 9/32, and adaptive variants project unsuccessful outcomes onto useful stabilizer states. The approach extends to larger GHZ measurements with exponentially higher success probability than previous linear-optical schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose linear-optical GHZ measurements using four-mode interferometers, reporting a 9/32 four-photon success probability and exponential gains for larger measurements.

entry.title: Unbounded gap between almost-quantum and commuting-operator correlations in zero-error communication
entry.summary: An Unbounded Separation of Almost-Quantum and Commuting-Operator Correlations in Zero-Error Communication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies a zero-error communication task in which Alice and Bob receive labels and Bob must decide whether the labels are equal, without ever erring but possibly abstaining. For every quantum model, the optimal probability of a conclusive answer is exactly 1/N, matching shared randomness. Almost-quantum correlations reach a success probability approaching 1/17, showing an unbounded separation from quantum correlations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that almost-quantum correlations are unboundedly stronger than quantum ones in zero-error equality communication, with closed-form SDP solutions across N and n-bit tasks.

entry.title: Almost-quantum correlations break information causality
entry.summary: Almost-Quantum Correlations Violate Information Causality arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether information causality, the principle that m classical bits cannot give a receiver more than m bits about the sender's independent data, holds for almost-quantum correlations. The authors show that these correlations violate information causality without bound. The violation is driven by zero-error certificates, which are rare but never wrong. The paper concludes that either information causality is a valid physical principle excluding these correlations, or no mutual information satisfying consistency, data processing, and the chain rule exists for theories realizing them. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show that almost-quantum correlations violate information causality without bound, using zero-error certificates, and discuss consequences for mutual information properties.

entry.title: Quantum query cost of checking whether a linear system is stable
entry.summary: Quantum query complexity of Hurwitz stability testing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how many quantum queries are needed to decide whether a matrix is Hurwitz stable, meaning all trajectories of the linear system converge to zero, given an exact block-encoding of the matrix. The complexity depends on the dimension n and a lower bound ν on the imaginary-axis distance. A lower bound of Ω(√n/ν) is proven even for real diagonal matrices. For Hermitian or normal matrices, an upper bound of O(√n ν⁻¹ log n) is given, matching the lower bound up to a logarithmic factor, while the general non-normal case has a weaker upper bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a quantum query lower bound Ω(√n/ν) for Hurwitz testing and an upper bound matching it up to a log factor for normal matrices, via projector block-encoding.

entry.title: A proof of the entropic c-theorem, a result on how a two-dimensional quantum field theory's central charge can be defined using entropy.
entry.summary: Proof of the entropic c-theorem arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proves an entropic c-theorem in two dimensions by building a c-function from the mutual information between spacelike separated wedges, defined via relative entropy. It follows Casini and Huerta's approach, replacing strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy with increasing differences of mutual information, proved directly in the continuum. Every quantity used is finite, so no cutoff is needed. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a two-dimensional entropic c-theorem using relative entropy and increasing differences of mutual information, avoiding any cutoff in the continuum.

entry.title: A general tensor-network method for hydrodynamics in higher dimensions
entry.summary: A Universal Approach to Hydrodynamics in Higher Dimensions via Tensor Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper extends the Density Matrix Truncation (DMT) algorithm to systems up to three dimensions to quantitatively predict high-temperature transport coefficients, such as diffusion constants, directly from microscopic quantum models. The authors also show the method can capture the slow crossover dynamics typical of weakly broken integrability. The approach preserves geometrically local information during time evolution, even though higher-dimensional calculations use a one-dimensional matrix product state ansatz. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend density matrix truncation to three dimensions, using 1D MPS to predict high-temperature transport coefficients and slow crossover dynamics.

entry.title: How rounding errors in low-precision SGD affect model scaling
entry.summary: Where, When, and How Many Bits? Scaling Laws for SGD with Stochastic Rounding arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper theoretically studies how stochastic rounding (SR) affects prediction risk in low-precision training as model size, training time, and precision change. It analyzes a two-layer linear network with a fixed random first layer, trained by mini-batch SGD on Gaussian data with power-law spectra, and proves matched upper and lower bounds on prediction error for the final model and for parameter averaging. Rounding only forward features preserves the compute scaling of exact arithmetic, while rounding backward features changes it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove matched upper and lower bounds for SGD with stochastic rounding, deriving scaling laws for compute, model size, and precision, checked on linear networks, MLPs, and a small transform

entry.title: ReplayRCA: Testing whether AI models can find and fix an agent's mistakes, either after a failure or while it runs
entry.summary: ReplayRCA: Measuring Post-hoc Diagnosis and Live Oversight of Agent Failures by Counterfactual Replay arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces ReplayRCA, a benchmark that scores diagnoses of language-model agent failures by intervention: the environment is reset, the proposed fix replaces the agent's action, and the agent continues. It has two tracks, post-hoc diagnosis of a failed run and live oversight that intervenes before an irreversible step. Tasks come from the OpsWorld back-office environment. The authors report that post-hoc diagnostic performance can be a poor predictor of live oversight ability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose intervention-based replay to score agent failure diagnoses, with post-hoc and live oversight tracks, testing 13 frontier models on 62 failures and 87 runs.

entry.title: Omniprediction for all mixable proper losses, a way to make predictions accurate under many loss measures at once
entry.summary: Omniprediction for All Mixable Proper Losses and Beyond arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies omniprediction in online learning, where predictions must perform well simultaneously under different loss functions. It shows that sublinear regret cannot be achieved for all bounded proper losses when the loss class is infinite, even with only two linear predictors. It then gives an algorithm achieving Õ(T^{1/3}(log|F|)^{2/3}) regret for all mixable proper losses, shown to be optimal up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show sublinear regret is impossible for all bounded proper losses, then give an near-tight T^{1/3} bound for all mixable proper losses, unifying known finite-class results.

entry.title: Can unlabeled pools replace membership queries for learning halfspaces?
entry.summary: When Can Unlabeled Data Pools Replace Membership Queries? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper asks when a learner that can only label sampled points can match the label efficiency of membership queries, which can label any point. For homogeneous halfspaces, the result depends on the angular distribution of X/||X||: if no hyperplane through the origin has mass and every open set of directions and its reflection has positive mass, a pool learner needs O(n log^3 n log(n/(εδ))) labels. The paper also gives separation results when these conditions fail and label-rate thresholds for isotropic s-concave marginals. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize when unlabeled pools can replace membership queries, giving logarithmic label bounds, separations, and tight bounds for isotropic s-concave marginals.

entry.title: Stronger retrievers, noisier labels: how incomplete relevance judgments distort abstention evaluation in conversational RAG
entry.summary: Better Retrievers, Worse Labels: How Incomplete Relevance Judgments Distort Abstention Evaluation in Conversational RAG arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how abstention is evaluated in conversational retrieval-augmented generation benchmarks. On RECOR, the authors test a shortcut that treats any context lacking gold documents as unanswerable, using four retrievers and three Qwen3 readers. They find that stronger retrievers yield more no-gold contexts that still contain the answer, which lowers the shortcut's precision; precision also drops on MTRAG. The authors recommend scoring refusals against content labels rather than gold-document presence. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that inferring answerability from incomplete relevance labels distorts evaluation, checked with content labels and a blind audit.

entry.title: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses
entry.summary: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies whether latent dynamics models learned for linear time-invariant systems can yield feedback controllers that stabilize the original system. Using linear autoencoders trained with multi-step prediction-reconstruction losses, the authors show that a long enough reconstruction horizon and sufficient latent dimension let an H-infinity controller designed on the latent model stabilize the original system via the encoder. The paper also explains why forward prediction losses and single-step reconstruction losses can fail to yield stabilizing controllers. Experiments on a non-linear flexible-arm system illustrate the implications for learning non-linear autoencoders. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that multi-step backward reconstruction losses yield latent models whose H-infinity controllers stabilize linear systems, and report experiments on a nonlinear flexible-arm system.

entry.title: Proof that Clifford circuit synthesis is NP-complete
entry.summary: Clifford synthesis is NP-complete arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that synthesizing a quantum circuit for a given Clifford operator within a specified resource budget is NP-complete under several practical resource models. It considers single-qubit and two-qubit Clifford gates with full qubit connectivity and no ancilla qubits. Building on work by Li and Guan, the authors give polynomial-time reductions from Hamiltonian path in grid graphs to these decision problems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove Clifford circuit synthesis is NP-complete across several resource models via polynomial reductions from grid Hamiltonian path, building on Li and Guan.

entry.title: Near-optimal first-order regret bounds for bandits with feedback graphs
entry.summary: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. Existing worst-case bounds depend on the graph's independence number, while the best prior first-order bounds depend on the clique partition number, leaving a gap between the two. The authors prove an expected regret bound of Õ(√(αL*)+α), where α is the independence number and L* is the cumulative loss of the best arm, closing this gap. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve first-order regret for feedback-graph bandits, replacing clique partition with independence number and extending to general strongly observable graphs.

entry.title: Learning finite-memory binary sources: estimating the statistical rules of short-memory bit sequences from one long data stream.
entry.summary: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how many samples are needed to estimate biased binary sources with finite memory from a single trajectory, a task relevant to entropy estimation in cryptography. It establishes sharp sample complexity bounds with matching upper and lower limits that do not depend on mixing time or spectral gap. The authors conclude that some published entropy-source validation trace lengths may be insufficient under these bounds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight sample complexity bounds for finite-memory binary sources using de Bruijn chain hitting times and majorization, questioning existing entropy-source validation trace lengths.

entry.title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
entry.summary: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper tests 281 imitation-learning robot policies from seven policy families in about 1,700 real-robot trials, using a five-fingered hand to grasp and insert RJ45 connectors. The results show that how observations and actions are represented matters far more than optimizer or sampling choices. Of 67 offline metrics, only five measures of predicted-motion smoothness and directness correlated with insertion success, and only within one policy family, so offline metrics can shortlist policies but cannot replace real-robot evaluation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare 281 imitation-learning policies in about 1,700 real-robot trials, isolating representation choices as key drivers of dexterous manipulation success.

entry.title: More rules, longer lists? Testing self-evolving agents on hidden rules
entry.summary: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces CLR-Bench, a benchmark for testing whether self-evolving agents can learn a hidden rule from feedback alone. Each chain adds one rule per level, and each rule applies to an opaque label that stands for a named grouping published on the Web. Six recent self-evolution methods barely learn with a certifying base model, but adding a fixed lesson stating the naming convention raises their scores by 14.5 to 16.5 points. With the stronger GPT-6-Sol, some methods learn from feedback alone. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce CLR-Bench, a hidden-rule curriculum benchmark; they report evaluating six self-evolution methods on 20 chains across 10 domains, finding performance differs across models.

entry.title: Bayesian power grid state estimation using flow matching
entry.summary: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses distribution system state estimation on medium-voltage feeders, which have few real-time measurements.
