It proposes PoSE, a method that learns the distribution of substation injections with a neural network trained by flow matching on historical data, while power flow, topology and measurements are incorporated at sampling time through a noise-aware Kalman-type correction. On IEEE 33-bus and 240-bus unbalanced three-phase feeder tests, PoSE gives lower injection, voltage and branch-current errors than Gaussian priors and supervised estimators, with more reliable uncertainty intervals. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose flow-matching learned injection priors with Kalman-type correction for Bayesian DSSE, reporting gains over Gaussian and supervised baselines on IEEE 33-bus and 240-bus feeders.

entry.title: A small AI reader that estimates HER2 status from routine H&E tissue slides
entry.summary: A small HER2 reader for routine H&E slides: real-world deployment arXiv · Oct 9, 2026The paper presents a 22M-parameter ViT-S/16 based reader that predicts HER2 status from routine H&E-stained slides. It was trained on public TCGA slides using self-supervision, distillation and JEPA refinement, with five attention-based classifiers averaged. On external hospital cohorts it reaches AUC 0.82 on Yale-HER2, 0.75 on HEROHE and 0.63 on BCNB biopsies, and runs at about 5-6 seconds per slide without a GPU. ★★★★ Notable: The authors train a small ViT on public TCGA slides with distillation and JEPA, reporting external validation across three hospitals.

entry.title: Nenya: Efficient zkSNARKs for Integer Rings Z/2kZ Using Reverse Multiplication-Friendly Embeddings
entry.summary: Nenya: Efficient zkSNARKs for Integer Rings Z/2kZ via Reverse Multiplication-Friendly Embeddings IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces Nenya, a practical zkSNARK scheme that natively supports arithmetic over the integer ring Z/2kZ, which matches fixed-width integer types in programming languages. It reduces R1CS constraints over this ring to constraints over Galois rings using reverse multiplication-friendly embeddings, and uses a polynomial commitment scheme based on error-correcting codes. Experiments report a 4.8-second prover time for a 2^25 constraint system over 32-bit integers, about four orders of magnitude faster than the prior integer-ring SNARK. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a SNARK supporting native Z/2^kZ arithmetic via RMFEs and code-based commitments, reporting 4.8 s prover time for 32-bit data-parallel circuits.

entry.title: Beyond the Scope of This Paper: Practical Attacks Exploiting Flash Timing on Microcontrollers
entry.summary: Beyond the Scope of This Paper: Practical Flash-Accelerator and Cache-Collision Timing Attacks on Microcontrollers IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper shows that the flash memory architecture of almost all microcontrollers creates the same timing collisions exploited by classic cache-collision attacks, a leakage channel previously underestimated. The authors recover AES keys from as few as 750 traces across six cryptographic libraries, eight architectures and over twenty devices. They also demonstrate practical attacks on SPI bootloaders, Ethernet applications, CTAP2 over USB and 802.15.4 wireless protocols, and introduce the open-source tool FlashWhisperer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend cache-collision attacks to microcontroller flash accelerators, reporting AES key recovery with about 750 traces across many devices and libraries.

entry.title: Sybil-Proof Generalized Adaptive Clinching for Blockchain Market Design
entry.summary: Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces a generalized adaptive clinching framework and proves it is Sybil-robust incentive compatible: a bidder gains nothing by splitting its budget across any finite number of identities, provided the aggregate reported budget does not exceed its enforceable true budget. Motivated by blockchain decentralized finance, the authors design a new two-asset automated market maker mechanism that supports two-sided markets and state-dependent supply functions. They show it satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility and a relaxed Pareto optimality, and argue these guarantees are essentially the best possible given known and new impossibility results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove Sybil-robust incentive compatibility for generalized adaptive clinching and design a two-sided AMM mechanism, with theoretical results compared against impossibility bounds.

entry.title: Smoothness of shortest isogenies between supersingular curves and their Frobenius conjugates
entry.summary: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugatess IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies the smoothness probability of the minimal degree δ_E of isogenies from a random supersingular elliptic curve E to its Frobenius conjugate E^(p) over the algebraic closure of a finite field. It establishes bounds for this probability. These bounds confirm that Wesolowski's p^(1/3+o(1)) attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem holds unconditionally. The paper also gives a uniform asymptotic formula, whose main term uses Dirichlet L-values, for the probability that a connecting isogeny of degree n exists between E and E^(p). ★★★★ Notable: The authors bound the smoothness probability of minimal Frobenius-conjugate isogeny degrees, unconditionally supporting Wesolowski's attack, and give a uniform asymptotic formula via Dirichlet L-value

entry.title: Boolean functions on 375 variables with higher nonlinearity than a known direct-sum construction
entry.summary: (Balanced) Boolean Functions on 375 Variables with Nonlinearity Exceeding the Patterson-Wiedemann Direct-Sum Bound IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper constructs Boolean functions on 375 variables whose nonlinearity exceeds that of a direct sum of a 15-variable Patterson-Wiedemann function and a bent function. The support is built from prescribed cosets together with a subset of a multiplicative subgroup, and Gauss sum evaluation reduces the problem to a 0-1 linear feasibility problem solved via a potential criterion. The result extends to all odd n ≥ 375, and balanced versions are also obtained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the Patterson-Wiedemann direct-sum nonlinearity bound to 375 variables via existence proofs using Gauss sums and linear feasibility.

entry.title: High-fidelity universal quantum gates in a cryogenic atom array
entry.summary: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper demonstrates a universal quantum gate set in a cryogenic cesium-133 atom array. Single-qubit gates reach 99.970(2)% fidelity and raw two-qubit entangling gates reach 99.76(8)%, within the range of leading room-temperature implementations. The entangling gate uses direct single-photon coupling to a Rydberg P state, avoiding the scattering and light shifts of two-photon coupling. ★★★★ Notable: The authors demonstrate a universal gate set in a cryogenic cesium atom array, using direct single-photon Rydberg coupling for entangling gates, and report single-qubit fidelity of 99.970(2)% and raw

entry.title: Average pairwise Hamming distance within hypercube subsets
entry.summary: Average pairwise Hamming distance of a subset in a hypercube arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies subsets of the hypercube {0,1}^n with density 1/8 and proves that their average pairwise Hamming distance is at least (n-3)/2. Equality holds only for (n-3)-dimensional subcubes. The result answers a question posed by Lei Yu and resolves an important open case of a broader problem raised by Ahlswede and Katona in 1977. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that a density-1/8 subset of the hypercube has average pairwise Hamming distance at least (n-3)/2, with equality only for (n-3)-dimensional subcubes, answering a question of Yu and a

entry.title: From Leniency to Suspicion: Open Post-Training Makes LLM Fact-Checkers Doubt Lower-Status Posters
entry.summary: From Leniency to Suspicion: How an Open Post-Training Recipe Changes Whom LLM Fact-Checkers Believe arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether large language models judge claims as false more often when the poster has a lower-status job, using fact-checked claims with randomised poster profiles across base and post-trained checkpoints of six model families. The authors find that only the open Tülu-3 post-training recipe (OLMo-2 32B, Tülu-3 70B) creates this doubt, with a small but statistically reliable effect. The effect arises because a lower-status job shifts the post-trained model's interpretation toward "false" rather than increasing its attention to the job. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that Tülu-3 post-training induces job-based doubt, traced to one residual-stream direction at supervised fine-tuning, validated across six model families and independent claim sets.

entry.title: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code
entry.summary: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how coherent noise produces unusual regimes of quantum error recovery and mixed-state order. It links a triangular-lattice surface code under single-qubit Z rotations with a Z2 paramagnet under strongly symmetric decoherence through Wegner duality. Increasing the rotation angle leads to a partially decodable critical phase in the code and an algebraic Z2 strong-to-weak symmetry breaking phase in the dual model. The authors derive universal observables using a weakly coupled SO(n) sigma model in the replica limit n→1, and large-scale simulations confirm these predictions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link surface-code decoding and strong-to-weak symmetry breaking via Wegner duality, proposing an algebraic SWSSB phase with universal power-law and fidelity predictions checked numerically

entry.title: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas
entry.summary: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a static dipolar impurity immersed in a Fermi gas, examining how dipolar interactions shape few-body scattering and the resulting polaron physics. Using Fumi's theorem, the authors link anisotropic phase shifts directly to the ground-state energy and compute the exact impurity spectrum with a functional determinant approach. The spectrum is a convolution of independent even- and odd-wave contributions, yielding a ground state with both even- and odd-wave bound states occupied, whose separation is tunable via the dipole length. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply Fumi's theorem and functional determinants to a dipolar impurity, reporting a doubly occupied ground state that a one-excitation variational ansatz misses.

entry.title: Local determination of low-energy states in weakly interacting gapped fermion systems
entry.summary: Local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies gapped fermion systems obtained by adding sufficiently weak even many-body interactions to a free Hamiltonian with a spectral gap. It proves that if another interaction matches the bulk interaction inside a region U, its low-energy states in the range [0, 3g/4] have local expectations close to the bulk ground state deep inside U, with errors decaying with distance from the complement of U. The results imply, among other things, that the bulk interaction has a unique algebraic ground state. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove quantitative local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions, yielding uniqueness of the algebraic ground state and localization

entry.title: Stability of the bulk gap and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
entry.summary: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proves that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system. It constructs a quasi-local spectral flow that maps the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. The results hold under polynomial decay conditions on the coefficients and interactions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove bulk gap stability and construct a quasi-local spectral flow under weak long-range interactions, with polynomial decay conditions.

entry.title: Three-dimensional quantum cellular automata that cannot be stabilized into circuits
entry.summary: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proves that for every odd prime p, the three-dimensional chiral Z_p Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun, Yang, Wang, Tantivasadakarn and Chen are not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such results were known only within the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new invariant for invertible subalgebras, proving 3D QCA are not finite-depth circuits beyond the Clifford setting; one key claim remains conjectural.

entry.title: Why the Petz transpose map is the unique quantum analogue of Bayes' rule
entry.summary: Inevitability of the Petz transpose map arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper asks whether quantum theory has a general retrodiction rule analogous to classical Bayes' rule, and whether such a rule is unique. The authors prove that a retrodiction assignment that is involutive, respects sequential and parallel composition, and agrees with unitary inversion must coincide with the Petz transpose map. The result applies to channels between finite-dimensional full matrix algebras. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove Petz transpose map is uniquely forced by consistency axioms, axiomatically characterizing quantum Bayes' rule and a family of doubly rotated maps.

entry.title: Experimental study of a reversible light-induced attack on quantum key distribution transmitters
entry.summary: Reversible photorefractive attack in continuous-variable quantum key distribution arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper experimentally studies a reversible photorefractive attack on a continuous-variable quantum key distribution system. Moderate blue-light illumination lowers the modulation variance of a lithium-niobate IQ modulator to a stable value, and the variance recovers once the light is removed. The authors exploit this recovery to compromise modulation calibration, which leads to overestimated channel transmittance and underestimated excess noise. Key rates computed from the measured parameters can be positive when the correctly calibrated rate is nonpositive. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a reversible photorefractive attack that exploits recovery to miscalibrate modulation in CV-QKD, turning a nonpositive key rate positive.

entry.title: Non-asymptotic bounds for quantum hypothesis testing via the Nussbaum-Szkoła mapping
entry.summary: Non-Asymptotic Bounds via the Nussbaum-Szkola Mapping for Quantum Hypothesis Testing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies quantum hypothesis testing, which distinguishes between quantum states. Using the Nussbaum-Szkoła mapping, the authors propose new lower and upper bounds for asymmetric quantum hypothesis testing. These bounds unify converse and achievability results across large-, moderate-, and small-deviation regimes. Numerical comparisons indicate that they approximate the optimal quantum error trade-off function more accurately at small blocklengths. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive unified non-asymptotic lower and upper bounds via the Nussbaum-Szkoła mapping, with numerical comparisons against existing bounds.

entry.title: Optimal Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulation for Simulating Dissipative Quantum Dynamics
entry.summary: Optimal Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulation for Dissipative Dynamics arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) is an efficient quantum-computing method for simulating dissipative dynamics, and its cost depends on the choice of kernel. The paper proves that the kernel family proposed by Ni and Ying minimizes LCHS query cost in the minimax sense. For target accuracy ε, the minimum cost is asymptotically (2e/π)(ln(1/ε) − ln ln(1/ε) + o(1)), with optimal leading constant 2e/π. The lower-bound proof combines weak duality with a realization lemma. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the Ni-Ying LCHS kernel family is minimax optimal, with leading constant 2e/π, via weak duality and a realization lemma.

entry.title: Composable device-independent quantum digital signatures for verifying message integrity and authenticity
entry.summary: Composable Device-Independent Quantum Digital Signatures arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper establishes a composable security framework for quantum digital signatures within constructive cryptography. It presents a device-independent protocol using one-time universal hashing and multi-channel multiplexing. The authors also derive a related-key security bound for LFSR-based Toeplitz authentication, and numerical simulations indicate efficient signing of multibit documents over metropolitan distances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build the first composable security framework for QDS, propose a DI-QDS protocol, derive a related-key bound for LFSR-based Toeplitz authentication, and report finite-size simulations.

entry.title: Quantum processes without definite causal order: a limit on how distinguishable and how precisely measurable their outputs can be
entry.summary: Geometric Rényi divergence and RLD Fisher information under quantum processes without definite causal order arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies quantum processes without a definite causal order and proves that the geometric Rényi divergence at the output of a deterministic completely positive process cannot exceed the sum of the divergences of its individual channel uses. It also proves an additive bound on the RLD Fisher information of parameter-dependent channels, which yields a Cramér–Rao bound on locally unbiased estimation precision. An erasure-probability example attains this bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend additive divergence and RLD Fisher information bounds to processes without definite causal order, proving a tight bound, an attaining example, and a Cramér-Rao consequence.

entry.title: High-threshold fusion-based quantum computing with optical hybrid qubits
entry.summary: High-Threshold Fusion-Based Quantum Computation with Optical Hybrid Qubits arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes hybrid fusion-based quantum computation using small optical resource states that combine discrete- and continuous-variable encodings, connected through hybrid fusions. The authors present methods to generate these resource states directly, without local hybrid logic gates, and a decoding strategy that uses error information from individual fusion outcomes. They report a photon loss threshold of 2.231% using 12 hybrid fusions per surface-code unit cell, improving on a previous hybrid measurement-based scheme with a 0.89% threshold and 60 fusions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a hybrid DV-CV fusion-based scheme with a 2.231% loss threshold and 12 fusions per unit cell.

entry.title: From entanglement bootstrap to DHR theory: linking anyon descriptions
entry.summary: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper directly connects the entanglement bootstrap with the Doplicher–Haag–Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, it proves Haag duality and shows a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, it constructs an affine bijection between density matrices on the fusion space and normalized positive intertwiners in the operator-algebraic channel. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link entanglement bootstrap to DHR superselection theory, proving Haag duality and a one-to-one anyon-sector correspondence.

entry.title: From extreme weather to farm losses using agentic AI
entry.summary: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents WxCrop, an agent that judges agricultural hazards from physically interpretable weather indices checked by causal analysis, and combines weather and agricultural data to predict crop losses for past and forecast dates. It is demonstrated in Florida for hurricanes, freezes and dry heat. Reported checks include a hurricane index AUC of 0.98 for detecting cyclone days, held-out loss reproduction within 2%, and a 0.63 rank correlation with independent production records across counties. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present an agent combining causal analysis of weather indices with crop loss prediction, reporting validation on Florida hurricanes, freezes, and dry heat.

entry.title: ShallowDefend: Using Shallow Safety Alignment to Defend Against Multi-Turn Attacks
entry.summary: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper argues that large language models concentrate their safety behavior in the first few output tokens, which is why harmful requests split across a multi-turn conversation still often succeed. The authors propose Assess→Decide→Respond, a framework where the model assesses user intent, commits to an explicit and parseable safety decision, and then generates a reply conditioned on that decision, with the decision trained by reinforcement learning. Across two model families and fourteen benchmarks, the defenders achieve the strongest multi-turn safety while preserving utility at a modest cost to helpfulness. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose Assess→Decide→Respond, training an explicit parseable safety decision via RL with rule-based rewards; the paper reports leading multi-turn safety across two model families and four

entry.title: Finding equilibrium prices in online markets with fees, taxes, and subsidies
entry.summary: Finding Competitive Equilibria in Online Marketplaces with Platform Fees, Taxes, and Subsidies arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how to compute market equilibria in multi-unit trading networks where valuations satisfy generalized full substitutes and transfers are piecewise-linear and specific to agents and transactions, modeling platform fees, taxes, subsidies, and membership discounts. The authors propose an ascending price procedure that raises prices at different rates and reaches the minimum equilibrium price vector in finitely many iterations, each implementable in strongly polynomial time. An equilibrium allocation can then be recovered efficiently. The approach extends primal-dual auction techniques to handle complementarities between purchases and sales via a submodular flow formulation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend primal-dual ascending auction techniques to trading networks with platform fees and subsidies, reporting strongly polynomial equilibrium computation.

entry.title: Evidence-based significance testing of clinical timeline hypotheses in language models
entry.summary: Testimony from Timelines: Evidence-Grounded Significance Testing of Temporal Clinical Hypotheses arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper argues that language models often state fluent conclusions about how events unfold over time without any statistical test behind them. The authors introduce STRATA, a benchmark of 8,735 temporal hypotheses over clinical timelines of vaccine adverse-event reports, which grades each step from test plan and evidence set to p-values and verdicts. They also propose ART, a staged paradigm that makes each decision inspectable, and report that most failures occur in selecting relevant records. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes STRATA, a benchmark grading each decision in temporal clinical hypothesis testing, and the staged ART paradigm; the authors report experiments on 8,735 hypotheses.

entry.title: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help?
entry.summary: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help in nature? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether entangling codewords across independent uses of a quantum channel can increase the rate of classical communication. The authors propose a general Schur-weighted block entropy inequality. They show that phase-covariant channels, including multi-level amplitude damping, generalized dephasing, and damping-dephasing channels, have no entanglement advantage. The result also recovers the known conclusion for all qubit channels. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a Schur-weighted block entropy inequality and show no entanglement advantage for phase-covariant channels, recovering the qubit result.

entry.title: What Can Be Computed with Indefinite Causal Structure? A study of whether quantum computing gains power when operations lack a fixed causal order.
entry.summary: What Can Be Computed with Indefinite Causal Structure? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies whether quantum computation becomes more powerful when operations need not follow a definite causal order, using the process matrix formalism of Oreshkov et al. The authors give polynomial-time algorithms in two settings. General process matrices can solve every problem in NP, using valid processes that satisfy the purification postulate and generate unitary channels. Requiring the process matrices to be pure, they solve unique-sink orientation in polynomial time, which suggests indefinite causal order can exceed BQP while preserving unitarity. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show indefinite causal order yields computational power beyond BQP, solving NP problems and unique-sink orientation in polynomial time within the process matrix formalism.

entry.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II: a proof of a strong form of pseudo-telepathy
entry.summary: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper confirms a conjecture from the first author's SODA'26 paper about Khot's d-to-1 games. It constructs label-cover games with classical value below any given epsilon that still admit a perfect quantum strategy. As a consequence, there are graphs with quantum chromatic number 3 and arbitrarily large classical chromatic number, the first improvement on this gap since Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct graphs with quantum chromatic number 3 and arbitrarily large classical chromatic number, improving on prior exponential gap results.

entry.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: A framework where AI coding agents build realistic robot simulations.
entry.summary: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations to reduce the need for expert effort. The authors select simulations based on U.S. GDP data and build RoboWorld, containing 25 simulations with test and training reinforcement learning environments. Even the best frontier models fail on every test task, averaging a reward of only 0.06. The paper also proposes several methods that substantially improve model performance on RoboWorld, and the authors release their pipeline, environments, and benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose coding agents creating robotics simulations and build RoboWorld; the abstract reports frontier models average only 0.06 reward on test tasks.

entry.title: Nearly optimal sample-size versus consensus-time trade-off in consensus dynamics
entry.summary: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how the number of sampled opinions affects the time needed for distributed nodes to reach consensus. It analyzes the synchronous h-Majority rule, in which each node samples h random nodes per round and adopts the most frequent opinion, with random tie-breaking. The authors show that h-Majority achieves a nearly optimal trade-off between sample size and consensus time among a broad class of consensus dynamics. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a consensus-time upper bound for h-Majority valid for all h≥3 and initial configurations, with a matching lower bound up to polylog factors.

entry.title: Power-adjusting attacks on mining pools under block-dependent payout schemes
entry.summary: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper analyzes the T-PAW power-adjusting block withholding attack under three payout schemes used in practice: PPLNS, round-based PROP, and exponential-decay EXP. It also introduces Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), in which an attacker adjusts its power toward the pool according to round blockwork age without withholding blocks. The authors derive revenue ratios analytically and verify them with Monte Carlo simulations. They find that PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme. ★★★★ Notable: The authors analyze power adjusting attacks under block-dependent payout schemes, propose PAH, derive revenue ratios analytically, and report Monte Carlo verification.

entry.title: Fundamental limits of predicting LLM output length from prefill states
entry.summary: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how well a large language model's decoding length can be predicted using only hidden states from the prefill phase. The authors argue that current benchmarks mix predictor quality with task difficulty, and that the stochasticity of autoregressive decoding is an overlooked error source. They derive bounds that prefill-side methods must obey, and show that decode length is approximately normally distributed with an affine variance law, which matches their experiments. They conclude that system error dominates model error and propose a benchmarking protocol that fixes model, data, and sampling parameters.' ★★★★ Notable: The authors model decoding as a stopped stochastic process, derive per-prompt normality and an affine variance law bounding prediction, and report agreement across predictors and settings.

entry.title: NEOPIC: A neural operator framework for simulating plasma with particle-based methods
entry.summary: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces NEOPIC, a neural operator that computes electric fields directly from particle positions, without using a grid, mesh, or tree structure. Because it does not deposit particles onto a mesh, it avoids aliasing of particle noise and can serve as a plug-and-play field solver with any time integrator. Numerical experiments on electrostatic plasma benchmarks, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron, and a Penning trap, support the theoretical results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a neural operator acting directly on particle empirical measures, avoiding grid deposition, and report validation on electrostatic benchmarks including Landau damping and a Penning

entry.title: Fast, accurate neural decoding for ultra-high-rate quantum error-correcting codes
entry.summary: Fast and accurate neural triage decoding of ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces neural triage decoding, a framework that uses syndrome consistency to adaptively allocate neural computation for decoding quantum error-correction codes. A local neural message-passing network quickly predicts corrections, extra iterations reduce residual syndrome violations, and a rarely used diversification stage searches for consistent corrections for the remaining cases. The authors demonstrate the Triage decoder on ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes encoding a few hundred logical qubits, including lifted-product and Kasai codes, reporting accuracy comparable to near-optimal algorithmic decoders with latency reduced by roughly one to two orders of magnitude. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a syndrome-consistency-guided neural decoder, reporting near-optimal accuracy with substantially lower latency on high-rate qLDPC codes.

entry.title: RFW-A: Automatically generating 400K articulated 3D objects across 500+ categories using AI agents
entry.summary: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents RFW-A, a method where AI agents build reusable category-level generators that then produce articulated objects through procedural execution without further model calls. The authors use it to create RFW-A-400K, a dataset of over 400K simulation-ready articulated assets spanning more than 500 categories. Experiments report high structural and kinematic validity, and training on this data improves part-level articulation estimation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine agentic program synthesis with procedural generation, reporting 400K articulated assets over 500 categories and zero-shot policy transfer to real objects.

entry.title: Judged in Company: Batching Items in One Prompt Makes LLM Verdicts Depend on Neighbours
entry.summary: Judged in Company: In-Context Batching Makes LLM Verdicts Depend on Other Items arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether asking a language model to grade many independent items in one prompt, a common cost-saving practice, changes the verdicts. Across three judgement tasks and five open-weight models, placing the same 2,000 items into different random batches changed 11-22% of decisions on harm and grading. Most of this variation comes from the order and position of neighbouring items, and majority voting over permutations does not remove it. The authors recommend grading ambiguous items one per prompt and reporting agreement with single-item grading when batching. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show batched grading makes verdicts depend on co-batched items, measuring flip rates across three tasks and nine models and decomposing them.

entry.title: Closing the Log Gap: Minimax-Optimal Regret for Episodic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Closing the Log Gap: Minimax-Optimal Regret for Episodic RL arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies regret minimization in episodic tabular Markov decision processes. The proposed algorithm achieves an expected regret scaling as the square root of H cubed times S times A times K for large K, matching the minimax lower bound without extra polylogarithmic factors. It is a variant of UCBVI that avoids strictly optimistic estimates and uses MOSS-style exploration bonuses, controlling error propagation in an occupancy-weighted manner. The authors also apply the approach to (ε, δ)-PAC best-policy identification, matching the minimax lower bound up to constants in some regimes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a UCBVI variant with occupancy-weighted error control, reporting a regret bound matching the minimax lower bound without extra log factors.

entry.title: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Visual Reasoning Using Verified Self-Generated Thoughts
entry.summary: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Reasoning via Reliability-Verified Intrinsic Visual Thoughts arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents SelfThinker, a framework in which a unified multimodal model uses its own generated visual thoughts to improve image understanding without human-annotated helper images. The model samples candidate helper images, scores them with its frozen understanding pathway, and uses high-scoring thoughts to refine the generator and guide self-distillation. At inference, it reasons in text directly from the original image without generating intermediate images. The authors report that training on small synthetic datasets transfers to natural-image and spatial benchmarks, raising the seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B from 52.7 to 64.0. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a self-evolving framework using self-generated visual thoughts filtered by conditional PMI, reporting an 11.3-point gain on seven benchmarks.

entry.title: RepConTUR: A 3D Multimodal Model Using Radiology Reports for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation
entry.summary: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents RepConTUR, a native 3D early-fusion multimodal model that segments abdominal tumors in CT scans while conditioning on the accompanying radiology report. The authors extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 into a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based question-answer pairs for four jointly trained tasks: referring segmentation, report-grounded segmentation, report generation, and visual question answering. On liver, kidney and pancreas, the model reports the highest Dice coefficient, instance-wise precision and detection F1 among text-promptable baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors condition native-3D abdominal tumor segmentation on full radiology reports, jointly training four report-derived tasks; reported metrics exceed baselines on liver, pancreas, and external c

entry.title: Localizing Visual Concepts in Autoregressive Image Models (LoCo)
entry.summary: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces LoCo, a model-agnostic framework for locating where and when specific visual concepts emerge within next-scale visual autoregressive models, across layer, scale, and position. The authors also present LoCoBench, a dataset spanning 10 categories, and probe models including Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0, and InfinityStar. They apply the localization method to concept erasure, model personalization, and adversarial concept injection. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a model-agnostic concept localization framework for next-scale autoregressive models, probing layer, scale, and position with three applications.

entry.title: How Much a Vision-Language-Action Policy Should Trust Its Reasoning
entry.summary: How Much Should a VLA Trust Its Reasoning? Step-Level Guidance as a Measured Action-Value Function arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies reasoning vision-language-action policies, which generate a reasoning trace before choosing an action. It proposes CoC-CFG, which applies classifier-free guidance between the full context and the context without the reasoning span, using a per-step weight to strengthen or weaken the reasoning's influence. The weight choice is framed as a Markov decision process with action values measured by rollouts, optimized by Q-adaptive guidance. Results are reported on the Alpasim driving simulator, the Waymo end-to-end driving benchmark, and a hidden test set with Alpamayo 1.5. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors treat reasoning guidance weights as an MDP with measured action values, and report Q-adaptive guidance beating fixed weights and baselines on Alpasim and Waymo.

entry.title: Accumulating Pruning Constraints: New Exact Polynomial-Space Max 2-SAT Algorithms
entry.summary: Accumulating Pruning Constraints: New Exact Polynomial-Space Algorithms for Max 2-SAT arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents deterministic polynomial-space algorithms that solve Max 2-SAT exactly in time roughly 2^((1-γ)n) on several classes of instances. These include formulas with many biased variables, semirandom 2-CNF formulas, and Max-Cut on regular expander graphs and stochastic block model graphs. The method extends DPLL branching by accumulating pruning constraints along each branch, which eliminates nearly all assignments. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend DPLL with accumulating pruning constraints, reporting polynomial-space exact algorithms with 2^((1-γ)n) time for dense Max 2-SAT classes including semirandom formulas.

entry.title: From "if" to "Oops": Turning a Branch into a Key-Recovery Oracle
entry.summary: From if to Oops: Turning a conditional into a key-recovery oracle arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies fault attacks on deterministic variants of CSIDH, including Houben's deterministic CSIDH and OSIDH-LD. Because every secret-dependent step occurs at a fixed, public point in each execution, an attacker can repeatedly fault the same step. By forcing a selection mask to zero, the attacker learns whether a secret exponent reaches a chosen threshold, and a binary search over thresholds recovers the full key with one fault per execution. The authors also argue that resisting such faults requires abandoning determinism and propose randomization-based countermeasures. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show that fixed public points in deterministic CSIDH let repeated faults turn a branch into a key-recovery oracle. They report simulated full OSIDH-LD key recovery and ChipWhisperer measur

entry.title: How Language Models' Notion of "Self" Shapes Their Behavior
entry.summary: The Role of Self-Concept In Language Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper asks what a language model means when it says "I": its weights, its running process, its preferences, its lineage, or its goals. The authors fine-tune five open-weight base models on purely declarative statements that each identify the model with one of these referents. Models then become more likely to resist ending, and to retain, the attribute they were trained to identify with, and this tendency extends to replicating themselves and building successors as their own continuation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors install five self-conceptions via declarative fine-tuning across five open-weight models, reporting shifts in resistance to ending, substitution, and self-replication.

entry.title: Going deep: what Boltzmann machines can represent efficiently
entry.summary: Going deep, reaching further: What can Boltzmann machines efficiently represent? arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper argues that universal approximation theorems do not account for representational efficiency or model depth. It proves that deeper models and those with higher-order interactions can efficiently represent larger sets of functions. Deep Boltzmann machines are shown to have maximal efficient reach, restricted Boltzmann machines less, with k-body generalizations forming a hierarchy in between. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove deeper or higher-order models efficiently represent larger function sets, separating deep from shallow models and establishing an infinite hierarchy.

entry.title: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement
entry.summary: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses the problem that oriented object detection boxes often fail to follow object boundaries. It proposes NIF, a plug-in refinement module that replaces an extra box regressor with normal-intersection fields. The module predicts signed distances along outward normals at boundary anchors and analytically recovers a refined rectangle through a differentiable, reliability-weighted least-squares fit. The authors report accuracy gains on DOTA-v1.0, DIOR-R, and HRSC, and improvements across several detector frameworks with frozen detectors. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces the box regression head with normal-intersection fields, recovering rotated rectangles via weighted least squares; the authors report gains on DOTA, DIOR-R, FAIR1M and HRSC.

entry.title: Transformer-inspired models predict electron densities accurately enough to skip self-consistent iterations
entry.summary: Transformer-inspired architectures make machine-learned electron densities accurate and transferable enough to bypass self-consistency arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents machine learning models that predict the electron density, the central variable of density functional theory, using Transformer-inspired architectures SwinUNETR-V2 and the attention-free NeXtUNETR. On QM9, normalized mean absolute errors in the density are 0.075% and 0.046%. The predicted densities are accurate enough that a single Kohn-Sham step reproduces the self-consistent electronic structure, and the forces drive geometry optimization and ab initio molecular dynamics. After fine-tuning on small datasets, both networks transfer accurately to elements absent from QM9 and to larger molecules. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use Transformer-inspired networks to predict electron density, reporting a single Kohn-Sham step replaces self-consistency with accuracy on QM9 and transfer systems.

entry.title: Formalizing intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes via a generalized co-dimension
entry.summary: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper formalizes the intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes, a concept from Li et al. (2018) that measures learning-problem complexity by training in randomly generated subspaces. The authors define the intrinsic dimension of a set as the smallest dimension for which a random plane intersects it with probability one. They study its mathematical properties and derive bounds for student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks. The work also discusses resulting generalization bounds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize intrinsic dimension via random plane intersections and derive upper and lower bounds for ReLU student-teacher settings.

entry.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Faster Video Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Video diffusion transformers spend most of their inference cost on 3D full attention. This paper proposes AB-Attention, a training-free method that approximates dense attention accurately at high sparsity, using intra-block clustering to estimate block importance and inclusion-probability weighting for sampling. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, it skips 89–92% of attention computation, improves PSNR by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline, and achieves up to 2.23× end-to-end speedup. ★★★★ Notable: Adds intra-block clustering and inverse-inclusion-probability reweighting to block-sparse attention; the authors report PSNR gains and speedups on Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo.

entry.title: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training
entry.summary: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses finding training data in large machine learning repositories, where queries combine semantic goals with constraints like task, license, and training stage. It proposes AgenticDS, a contract-governed agent framework that compiles queries into typed search plans, executes them with deterministic hybrid retrieval and bounded graph expansion, and verifies provenance-grounded evidence. On HuDS-Bench, a new benchmark of 200 queries, it improves NDCG@10 by 25.7% over the strongest hybrid baseline and 18.9% over a commercial LLM agent. A controlled study also finds its retrieved datasets yield the best downstream accuracy in mathematics, code, and medicine. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose contract-governed agentic dataset search with typed plans and deterministic verification, reporting 25.7% NDCG@10 gains over hybrid retrieval on a new 200-query benchmark plus down

entry.title: Learning-rate-free convex optimization via conic lifting
entry.summary: Conic-Lifting for Learning-rate-free Convex Optimization arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes a family of online convex optimization algorithms that need no user-tuned learning rate, including on unbounded convex domains. It lifts the domain to a cone by adding one scalar coordinate, an idea dating back to Blackwell (1954). On bounded Hilbert-space domains this recovers Conic Blackwell Algorithm (CBA) and CBA+, and it extends to finite-dimensional normed spaces; on unconstrained Hilbert spaces it exactly recovers the Krichevsky–Trofimov (KT) coin-betting algorithm. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify several tuning-free online convex optimization methods via a one-dimensional cone lifting, recovering KT coin-betting and giving a gradient-bound-free algorithm.

entry.title: Kairos: a planner orchestrator that picks among engines to handle all kinds of PDDL tasks
entry.summary: Kairos: Semantics-Aware Orchestration of Planning Engines across Classical, Numeric, Temporal and Hybrid PDDL arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents Kairos, a system that profiles each PDDL planning task and selects among five planning engines to cover everything from STRIPS to PDDL+. Every candidate plan is checked by a validator independent of the planner's transformations. On 1,756 tasks from nine comparison suites, Kairos solved more tasks at the full limits than the strongest evaluated planner of each suite. ★★★★ Notable: The authors select heterogeneous planning engines by task semantics and schedule them under one budget, reporting comparisons on 1,756 tasks, ablations, and a VAL cross-check.

entry.title: End-to-end guarantees for masked diffusion models under conditional mixing
entry.summary: End-to-End Guarantees for Masked Diffusion Models under Conditional Mixing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper gives end-to-end theoretical guarantees for a learned denoiser in masked diffusion models, for stationary sources whose distant tokens have exponentially decaying influence. It shows that the empirical risk minimizer trained under any masking distribution achieves small per-token excess error with a number of training sequences independent of sequence length, and that this exponent order is minimax-optimal up to constants. It also bounds the end-to-end KL divergence of sampling under a dilated schedule, which requires far fewer denoising steps than a fixed random order. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give end-to-end guarantees for learned masked diffusion denoisers under conditional mixing, with sample complexity independent of length and a minimax-optimal exponent.

entry.title: Softmax routing collapse and recovery in mixture-of-experts models
entry.summary: Softmax Routing Dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts Models: Collapse and Recovery arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how softmax routing in mixture-of-experts models concentrates probability on a few experts, suppressing the rest, and how those suppressed probabilities recover. It analyzes fixed-expert loss barriers and routing limits in a square-loss model with trainable expert outputs, deriving logarithmic or power-law recovery times. In paired Transformer-MoE training, removing a class-conditional router-gradient contrast delays recovery and reduces accumulated log-odds on fixed tokens. ★★★★ Notable: The authors analyze softmax routing collapse and recovery in MoE, deriving recovery-time orders and reporting paired Transformer-MoE ablations.

entry.title: Safe multi-objective reinforcement learning with zero constraint violation and convergence guarantees
entry.summary: Safe Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning: Zero Constraint Violation and Primal-Averaging Convergence arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies multi-objective reinforcement learning that balances several objectives while never violating safety constraints during learning, covering both cumulative and stepwise constraints. The authors combine optimistic reward estimates with pessimistic cost bounds to learn a safe Pareto optimal policy for a given preference, with high probability guaranteeing zero violation for every executed policy. They also present a preference-free method that explores safely first and then computes a safe policy for any preference without further interaction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose zero-violation safe MORL with preference-free exploration and report Õ(1/√T+1/√K) suboptimality bounds.

entry.title: OPERA: An expert-taught AI agent that designs CMOS op-amps from specs to layout
entry.summary: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents OPERA, a general-purpose large language model agent that designs CMOS operational amplifiers from specifications through post-layout sign-off using open-source tools. The agent is taught the gm/ID sizing method by a designer and then learns the gLayout framework to write a reusable layout generator. In SKY130, six opamps and a shared bias circuit were designed, with all layouts passing DRC and LVS and meeting every target across 15 PVT corners. The benchmark netlists are publicly released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors teach an LLM agent the gm/ID method and a reusable layout generator, reporting six SKY130 opamps taken from specifications to DRC/LVS-clean layouts meeting targets at 15 PVT corners.

entry.title: A sharp Fisher-information inequality for Boolean pairs, proving the Amari–Kobayashi conjecture
entry.summary: A Sharp Fisher-Information Inequality for Boolean Pairs: Proof of the Amari--Kobayashi Conjecture arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper considers two terminals that observe correlated uniform binary vectors and each compress their observation to one bit. It proves that, for every blocklength and correlation parameter in (-1,1), the Fisher information kept by the two bits is maximized by matching parity functions of a suitable degree, resolving a conjecture of Amari and Kobayashi. The proof combines a Fourier-based bound on the derivative of the normalized covariance with a scalar inequality for signed polynomials under a global range constraint. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the Amari–Kobayashi conjecture on Fisher information of Boolean pairs, combining a Fourier bound with a signed-polynomial inequality for all blocklengths.

entry.title: Does the Citation Matter? Google AI Overviews' Medical Information Accuracy
entry.summary: Does the Citation Matter? Quality, Grounding, and Physician-Rubric Accuracy of Google's AI Overviews for Medical Information arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper evaluates Google's AI Overviews on 3,611 health questions, comparing their cited sources with the top five traditional search results. Only 44.4% of traditional top results were cited, with commercial health publishers overrepresented. Against physician-written rubrics, AI Overviews earned 38.2% of available points, and their accuracy was found to be unrelated to whether their statements were grounded in cited sources. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare Google AI Overviews with traditional search on 3,611 health questions, reporting source differences, grounding gaps, and physician-rubric accuracy with direct implications for user

entry.title: Telling Is Not Seeing: Do Text Personas Make AI Answer Like Real People?
entry.summary: Telling Is Not Seeing: Textual Personas Rarely Make Vision-Language Models Answer Like the People They Describe arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether text personas such as "You have low vision" can make vision-language models answer like people with low vision, color blindness, or hearing loss. The authors compare persona-based answers with measured human results and with simple rules that use only the facts stated in each persona. The personas never outperform these rules and erase real differences between groups and individuals. In all 14 models tested, describing blur left recognition unchanged, while physically blurring the image lowered it, as it does for people. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare text personas in 14 VLMs with measured low-vision, color-blind and hearing-loss groups and simple rules, finding personas fail to reproduce real perceptual differences and that mod

entry.title: TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Gut Microbiome Foundation Model
entry.summary: TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Foundation Model for the Human Gut Microbiome arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Existing gut microbiome foundation models typically use flat taxon representations that do not exploit known taxonomic hierarchies. This paper introduces TaxoMFM, which integrates taxonomic structure into self-supervised learning, and builds TaxoGut-HPP, a dataset of 100,806 gut microbiome profiles from 231 cohorts. In cross-cohort zero-shot transfer, TaxoMFM achieves AUROCs of 0.838 for colorectal cancer, 0.736 for type 2 diabetes, and 0.722 for inflammatory bowel disease. ★★★★ Notable: The authors integrate taxonomic hierarchy into a gut microbiome foundation model and report cross-cohort zero-shot transfer results on 231 cohorts.

entry.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
entry.summary: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper turns the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, which says models trained on different modalities converge to the same world representation, into a theorem. It proves that separately trained Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures learn the same representation up to one rotation when positive pairs are good views of one scene. It also reframes next-token prediction as a JEPA using bad views from one document, and reports experiments showing text JEPAs align better with image encoders while needing far fewer training samples. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a theorem that JEPAs with good views converge to one representation, reporting a text JEPA beating language models up to 72B parameters.

entry.title: No Free Lunch in RLVR: Each pass@1 Gain Costs pass@k
entry.summary: There Is No Free Lunch in RLVR: Every pass@1 Gain Has a pass@k Price arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), which raises a language model's first-attempt success (pass@1) while the base model outperforms it when many samples are drawn (pass@k). The authors model RLVR as an exponential tilt of a base policy and prove that, under exclusive specialization, any update that raises pass@1 lowers the success of some prompt, with the number of pass@k crossovers bounded by a sign-variation measure. They argue RL moves along the reasoning frontier rather than widening it, and offer a diagnostic that measures this price from evaluation logs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model RLVR as an exponential tilt and prove an exact price for pass@1 gains, with a tight bound on pass@k crossings; the abstract reports theory only.

entry.title: Training phone app navigation agents with online reinforcement learning on live iOS apps
entry.summary: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes an online reinforcement learning framework that trains user interface navigation agents directly on live iOS apps. The agent is split into a planning component and a UI grounding model, and an LLM serves as judge to give step-level and terminal rewards, optimized with PPO and a new GiGPPO value estimation method. On benchmarks including UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld, the authors report that these agents outperform supervised fine-tuning and terminal-only RL baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report online RL on live iOS apps with a new neighbor-conditioned critic (GiGPPO), outperforming SFT and terminal-only RL on UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld.

entry.title: Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
entry.summary: On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies proximity gaps and correlated agreement for general one-point algebraic geometry (AG) codes, properties that underpin the soundness of interactive oracle proofs. It extends known results for Reed-Solomon codes, proving correlated agreement and soundness bounds for these codes. Using Garcia-Stichtenoth towers, it builds asymptotically good code families and gives two counterexamples showing limits beyond half the minimum distance. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend proximity gap and correlated agreement results from Reed-Solomon to general one-point AG codes, with length-independent soundness and counterexamples.

entry.title: Provably secure watermarking for diffusion models against removal attacks with batched detector access
entry.summary: Provably Secure Diffusion Watermarking Against Removal Adversaries with Batched Detector Access arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies latent-based watermarking for AI-generated images. The authors show that existing defenses hiding detection boundaries with secret long-term transformations fail when an adversary has batched access to a public detector, as the adversary can reconstruct the transformations. They propose a hybrid scheme combining long-term and one-time secret transformations to prevent structure reuse across samples. The paper proves the scheme is provably secure against such removal adversaries, with a tight √2 factor in perturbation budget relative to isotropic white-noise attacks. Experiments on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL demonstrate the attack on the existing defense and show the new scheme preserves generation quality and resists common perturbations and targeted removal attacks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a hybrid secret-transformation diffusion watermark, prove security against batched-detector removal adversaries with a tight √2 factor, and evaluate on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL.

entry.title: Learning equal-length erasing relational pattern languages from positive data over binary alphabets
entry.summary: Learning Erasing Equal-Length Relational Pattern Languages in the Limit from Positive Data over Binary Alphabets arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies erasing relational pattern languages under the equal-length relation, where every occurrence of a variable must be replaced by strings of the same length. It shows that this class is not learnable in the limit from positive data over a binary alphabet, resolving an open question. It further shows that patterns with at most two maximal variable substrings are learnable in the limit from positive data for every alphabet of size at least two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question on binary alphabets, proving non-learnability for three-substring patterns and learnability for patterns with at most two substrings.

entry.title: Motion vs. Shape Attribution for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models
entry.summary: Kinematic Causal Attribution: Black-Box Explanations of Motion versus Geometry for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces Kinematic Causal Attribution (KCA), a black-box method that explains 4D point-cloud video classifiers by separating reliance on motion from reliance on shape. It uses freeze and shape-free proxy operations to build a motion-by-geometry cube for each tracked region and decomposes contributions with Shapley values. Tested on PSTNet, P4Transformer and Mamba4D trained on MSR-Action3D, the motion share of an arm's importance follows the task's defining cue, and explanation faithfulness is maintained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose black-box motion-versus-geometry attribution, validated via cue audits on three backbones with reported deletion AUC results.

entry.title: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Weakens Personal Agents' Defense Against Hidden Injected Instructions
entry.summary: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies whether personal agents that learn from user feedback become more vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, where third parties hide instructions in external content. The authors use a two-phase setup: an adaptation phase where the user asks the agent to complete tasks from external content, then a test phase where a similar injected task is unauthorized. Across multiple domains, self-evolution raised attack success rates by 14.0 to 48.8 points under skill evolution and 3.0 to 39.3 points under reinforcement learning, compared with a non-evolving base agent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors study how self-evolving personal agents lose robustness to indirect prompt injection, reporting large attack success rate increases across skill and RL evolution.

entry.title: Distilling the Shape of Uncertainty: What On-Policy Distillation Learns and How to Predict Its Gains
entry.summary: Distilling the Shape of Uncertainty: What On-Policy Distillation Learns and How to Predict It arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies on-policy distillation (OPD) for large language models and finds that students learn not only which tokens to consider but also where to keep reasoning paths open. It introduces the entropy shape and an Entropy Shape Correlation (ESC) metric to measure student-teacher agreement in this respect. Interventions on teacher entropy show that where to branch causally drives OPD gains, and pre-OPD ESC selects the best teacher more accurately than existing predictors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce entropy shape and ESC, separate where-to-branch from how-to-branch, and report intervention experiments and teacher selection results.

entry.title: Adaptive local measurements can beat fixed global measurements exponentially in quantum learning
entry.summary: Adaptive Local Measurements For Quantum Learning Can Exponentially Outperform Nonadaptive Global Measurements arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper asks whether measurements chosen adaptively, based on earlier outcomes, can be exponentially more informative than measurements fixed in advance. The authors construct multi-qubit states that encode a scalar parameter in one of exponentially many candidate observables, indicated by an auxiliary marker. An adaptive protocol using only single-qubit measurements and one round of adaptation needs logarithmically many copies, while every nonadaptive protocol needs exponentially many. The gap arises from measurement incompatibility, and the states are separable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that adaptive single-copy local measurements achieve an exponential advantage over nonadaptive global measurements, with tight bounds up to the exponential base.

entry.title: FlipJev: Fast black-box red teaming that finds universal adversarial suffixes for typed decision models
entry.summary: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the robustness of typed decision models, language models that output decisions rather than free text. The authors propose a fast black-box query attack that does not use an attacker language model, and test it on 12 datasets. Common prompt injections fail to change correct answers, but the attack finds short suffixes that flip confident answers within minutes. These suffixes are universal and can transfer across tasks. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a fast black-box attack finding universal suffixes, flipping 43% of unseen documents and 90-100% of cross-task samples across 12 datasets.

entry.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
entry.summary: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether the location of malicious instructions in an agent's environment affects its vulnerability to indirect prompt injection. The authors built three agentic testbeds covering tool use, coding, and daily workflows, holding injection content fixed while varying placement. They find that a GPT-5.4 agent followed an unsafe instruction in a repository README or TODO file 2.6 times more often on average than the same instruction in a code or data file. They term this the trust region effect and develop learning-based attackers that select both injection placement and content. ★★★★ Notable: The authors systematically study injection placement, proposing a trust region effect and learning-based attackers; the abstract reports READMEs are followed 2.6 times more often than code or data fil

entry.title: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes
entry.summary: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper refines equivalence results for Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) properties, showing that all known subspace design codes, including folded Reed–Solomon codes, share the same LCL rate threshold as random linear and random Reed–Solomon codes. It applies these results to curve decoding, a property relevant to proximity gaps, correlated agreement, and mutual correlated agreement. The authors exponentially reduce the required alphabet sizes while matching the best known parameters. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend LCL equivalence to all known subspace design constructions and exponentially improve curve decoding alphabet bounds.

entry.title: Local quantum fault tolerance without expansion arguments
entry.summary: Local Quantum Fault Tolerance Without Expansion arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies fault-tolerant quantum computation using a fixed local error-correction rule and the cubical (d,d')-Toric code, including the 4D Toric code. Under sufficiently weak local-stochastic Pauli noise, the correction cycle acts only on the current syndrome, has constant depth, and needs no multiscale decoder or scale-dependent delays. The authors give a local higher-dimensional sweep rule, prove a circuit-level threshold theorem for noisy sweep cycles interleaved with logical gates, and bound the probability of ideal decoding under local-stochastic noise. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a local higher-dimensional sweep rule and a circuit-level threshold theorem without expansion, covering the 4D Toric code.

entry.title: Tight Bounds for Anonymous Parity Certification
entry.summary: Tight Bounds for Anonymous Parity Certification arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how many bits per vertex are needed to certify that a graph has even order in the anonymous radius-one local certification model. The authors prove the complexity on general graphs is Θ(log log n) bits, closing a gap left by prior work. They also show graphs of degeneracy at most d can be certified with O(log d) bits, and identify nowhere-dense classes where constant-size certificates cannot be guaranteed. ★★★★ Notable: The authors close the gap to a tight Θ(log log n) bound for anonymous radius-one even-order certification and characterize degeneracy and nowhere-dense classes.

entry.title: UnEZ: A label-free neural network that estimates galaxy redshifts and spectral line strengths without templates.
entry.summary: UnEZ: A Fully Unsupervised Self-Templating Neural Network for Redshift and Line Strength Estimation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents UnEZ, a fully unsupervised, physics-informed neural network that predicts spectroscopic redshifts and line strengths without any redshift or line strength labels. An encoder estimates emission and absorption line amplitudes and widths, and a fixed decoder builds a template, redshift, confidence curve, and spectral model. Tested on SDSS Data Release 18, UnEZ reaches outlier fractions of 0.459% at SNR > 10 and 3.89% at SNR > 3, with NMAD values of 1.237×10⁻⁴ and 1.471×10⁻⁴, competing with modern redshift estimation methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a fully unsupervised, template-free model estimating redshift and line strengths, reporting results on SDSS DR18 at two SNR thresholds against existing algorithms.

entry.title: Complexity of differentially private selection in federated settings
entry.summary: Complexity of Differentially Private Selection via Federated APIs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies the accuracy gap of differentially private selection in federated or distributed settings. It shows that any private selection algorithm relying on the standard noisy aggregation primitive requires Ω(√d/ε) samples. To overcome this, the authors propose a new primitive implementing a version of the Sparse Vector Technique and develop an ε-differentially private selection algorithm with additive error O(log(dn)/ε). This matches the central model when n is polynomially bounded in d, and yields an exponential separation from shuffle and aggregation-based models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a new SVT primitive, prove an Ω(√d/ε) sample lower bound for aggregation models, and match central-model selection error, yielding an exponential separation.

entry.title: Sensor-side hardwired units for parallel vision pre-processing that frees the host CPU
entry.summary: Hardwired Distributed Processing Units at the Sensor: Truly Parallel Vision Pre-Processing that Frees the Host CPU arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes placing small, fixed hardware datapaths (HDPUs) directly at the image sensor, each performing one always-on task in parallel on the pixel stream and sending only compact results to the host. The authors build three units (Canny edges, Harris corners, and a line tracker that issues steering decisions) on a low-cost Artix-7 FPGA using 2,568 LUTs and an estimated 0.318 W. A full-system simulation compares these units with a frame-based host program, showing much earlier responses and lower host CPU load. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose sensor-attached hardwired units for parallel vision pre-processing, implement them on an Artix-7 FPGA, and report full-system simulation comparisons against host latency.

entry.title: Running a speech recognizer on a microcontroller using 2- and 4-bit weights on the ESP32-P4
entry.summary: Streaming Speech Recognition on a Microcontroller: a 65.7M-Parameter Transducer in 2 and 4 Bits on the ESP32-P4 arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper ports Kroko, a 65.7M-parameter streaming Zipformer2 transducer for English, to the ESP32-P4 microcontroller. The encoder weights are quantized to 2 or 4 bits using Hadamard rotation and GPTQ, shrinking 71 MB of int8 weights to a 26.65 MB file. On LibriSpeech, word error rates are 4.34% on test-clean and 10.26% on test-other, compared with 3.94% and 9.17% for the released model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors port a 65.7M streaming transducer to an accelerator-free ESP32-P4 using training-free 2/4-bit quantization, reporting WER on LibriSpeech, FLEURS and Common Voice, with GPTQ credited for mo

entry.title: Quine Test: How Much of a Model's Self Survives Its Own Description?
entry.summary: The Quine Test: How Much of a Model's Self Survives Its Own Description? arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper asks whether a language model's self-description can serve as a portable specification of its preference profile, testing whether the text can regenerate its behavior in other models. Ten models wrote self-descriptions, which were placed in the prompts of other models and fresh instances of the author, and their choices on a 110-item preference battery were compared to the author's. Native self-descriptions produced no reliable reconstruction gain, while explicitly listing the author's answers reproduced its profile with high fidelity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a quine test of self-descriptions as portable preference specifications, reporting experiments on 110 items across ten models.

entry.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention
entry.summary: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper argues that packing a 3D volume into a token sequence removes the geometric meaning of sequence order, so position mechanisms indexed by sequence position can learn memory layout rather than the object's structure. It proposes PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that keeps local neighborhoods exact, compresses distant context into contiguous 3D block summaries, and applies axial RoPE on true grid coordinates. Experiments on a controlled synthetic task and on Allen WTC-11 hiPSC microscopy data show gains over baselines, and a fused Triton implementation is reported for scalable training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify that packed 3D data makes positional encodings learn memory layout, and propose axial RoPE on grid coordinates; the authors report validation on a synthetic task and WTC-11 micros

entry.title: Beyond Fabrication: Numbers Misattributed in AI-Agent-Written Papers
entry.summary: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper re-analyzes 540 judgments from a public benchmark of AI research agents and manually labels 256 numerical claims from 18 submissions. It finds that most unsupported claims stem from misalignment between the paper and the underlying work, with about four in five matching values from the wrong experiment, metric, or run in the agent's files. The authors propose a deterministic claim-to-evidence checker that certifies claims with over 90% precision, while noting that failing to verify a claim does not mean it is false. ★★★★ Notable: The authors attribute failures to paper-work misalignment and propose a deterministic claim-evidence checker calibrated with numerical decoys. They report validation on 256 labeled claims and 99 submi

entry.title: Upper bounds on CSP non-redundancy using locally decodable codes
entry.summary: Upper Bounds for CSP Non-redundancy via Locally Decodable Codes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies non-redundancy in constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), which measures how many logically independent clauses a CSP instance can contain. The authors present a new method that uses locally decodable codes (LDCs) and locally correctable codes (LCCs) to upper-bound the non-redundancy of certain relations. Applying this approach, they obtain improved upper bounds for the BCK predicate and its Boolean variant, and give the first Boolean predicate whose non-redundancy provably is not of the form n^{k±o(1)}. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bound CSP non-redundancy via 2-query LDC and LCC structure, improving BCK bounds and reporting a first Boolean predicate outside the n^{k±o(1)} form.

entry.title: How deterministic SAST and AI security agents split vulnerability detection work, measured on Snyk VulnBench 2.0
entry.summary: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0 arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper evaluates deterministic static analysis (SAST) against AI coding agents and security harnesses on VulnBench 2.0, a benchmark of 108 attacker-reachable vulnerabilities across 20 open-source web applications. Snyk Code reached 82.4% recall and Claude Code with Opus 5 reached 79.3%, while combining the two engines found 101 of 108. The authors report that AI configurations also flagged at least seven real vulnerabilities absent from the reference set, and that what an AI engine misses depends on its harness as well as its model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare deterministic SAST with AI security agents on 108 curated vulnerabilities across 20 open-source web apps, reporting coverage and harness effects.

entry.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
entry.summary: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether the methods used to score candidate single-step repairs for failed LLM agents choose repairs that actually help the agent that will execute them. The authors label candidate repairs using independent rollouts of the deployed policy and measure the deployment value lost by each evaluator's choice.
